summary: Re-confirm industry methylation-data approaches organized by 4 user axes (tag-cluster-then-compare / read-level distance / site-level difference / discrimination) + difficulties, mapped to ISM
logs: Re-confirming 4 axes + canonical-pipeline + cross-difficulties (web-verified), waves of ~4

axes.axis: AXIS 1 — Tag/Haplotype-first methylation comparison (phase SNVs -> haplotag reads -> per-haplotype methylation -> compare HP1 vs HP2 mean methylation / DMR). The DOMINANT industry approach for ONT long-read allele-specific / haplotype-resolved methylation.
axes.canonical_workflow: Canonical 5-stage pipeline: (1) PHASE germline heterozygous SNVs into haplotype blocks with WhatsHap / Clair3(+WhatsHap) / longphase (co-phases 5mC) -> phased VCF with PS phase-set + GT pipe. (2) HAPLOTAG reads: assign each read HP:Z:1 or HP:Z:2 by matching its alleles at het SNVs to a haplotype block (whatshap haplotag / longphase haplotag); reads spanning no het SNV stay untagged. (3) SPLIT methylation: each read carries MM/ML modification tags (5mC, optionally 5hmC) and inherits its HP tag, so per-CpG methylation calls partition into HP1 vs HP2 piles (NanoMethPhase methyl_call_processor, modkit pileup --partition-tag HP / --phased, pycoMeth read-groups in MetH5). (4) PER-HAPLOTYPE methylation frequency: at each CpG compute beta = N_mod/(N_mod+N_canon) separately for HP1 and HP2 (one bedMethyl per haplotype). (5) COMPARE HP1 vs HP2: per-CpG significance test + region aggregation -> allelically differentially methylated regions (aDMRs / ASM). The reported effect is Delta-beta = mean(HP1) - mean(HP2) per site/region; canonical significance is the DSS Wald test (NanoMethPhase) or modkit's likelihood-ratio / MAP p-value, BH-FDR corrected, region call gated on |Delta-beta| >= 0.1 plus a min-CpG / min-coverage threshold. In CANCER the somatic refinement adds a normal/germline control to subtract imprinting + random monoallelic ASM, and uses copy-number/LOH-aware phasing because tumors lose het anchors.

tools.name: NanoMethPhase (+ DSS dma module)
tools.what_it_does: Reference haplotype-methylation tool. Takes phased VCF + alignment + Nanopolish (or modbam) methylation calls; separates reads & their CpG methylation to HP1/HP2; outputs phased methylation-frequency files; the 'dma' module wraps the DSS R package to call differentially methylated loci/regions between the two haplotypes (mono-allelic / ASM detection).
tools.statistic: Per-CpG (DML) = DSS DMLtest: empirical-Bayes beta-binomial with log-normal-prior dispersion SHRINKAGE + spatial SMOOTHING of mean methylation, then a WALD test per site (z = Delta-beta / SE); DMR = merge significant adjacent DMLs (callDMR). Output callDML.txt (per-locus), callDMR.txt (region), DMLtest.txt (all-loci). Effect = per-CpG/region mean methylation difference between haplotypes; multiple-testing via DSS/BH.
tools.granularity: Both: DML = per-CpG single-locus; DMR = region (adjacent significant loci merged).
tools.cancer_or_germline: Tool is germline/allele-generic (built for mono-allelic ASM); HP1-vs-HP2 axis = GERMLINE allelic axis. Used in cancer cohorts (POG) but somatic specificity needs an external normal/imprinting filter.
tools.platform: ONT long-read; Nanopolish or modbam (MM/ML) methylation input.
tools.citation: Akbari V. et al., 'Megabase-scale methylation phasing using nanopore long reads and NanoMethPhase', Genome Biology 2021;22:68. PMID 33618748; DOI 10.1186/s13059-021-02283-5. DSS: Park & Wu, Bioinformatics 2016;32(10):1446, DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btw026.

tools.name: modkit pileup --phased / --partition-tag HP + modkit dmr (pair/multi)
tools.what_it_does: Oxford Nanopore official Rust toolkit. 'pileup' reads MM/ML tags directly from modBAM and, with --phased / --partition-tag HP, emits one extended-bedMethyl per haplotype (HP1, HP2, ungrouped). 'modkit dmr pair' (or 'multi' for >2) scores differential methylation between the two haplotype bedMethyls; optional HMM '--segment' discovers regions de novo.
tools.statistic: Regions: log MARGINAL LIKELIHOOD-RATIO score = log[ l_thetaA(Xa)*l_thetaB(Xb) / l_thetaA+B(Xa+b) ] under Beta-Binomial (2-state) or Dirichlet-Multinomial (5mC/5hmC/C) posterior with Jeffreys prior (separate-vs-pooled model fit). Single base: likelihood-ratio score + MAP-based p-value p = f(0)/f(Delta), Delta = phat1-phat2, Z=Beta(a1,b1)-Beta(a2,b2). Effect size: Cohen's h (proportion diff) with 95% CI for regions/segments. Reads modBAM natively, no bisulfite assumption.
tools.granularity: Both: single CpG (dmr pair single-base) and region (BED-provided or --segment HMM).
tools.cancer_or_germline: Generic between-group; HP1-vs-HP2 = germline allelic axis. Modern default for ONT cancer methylation pileups.
tools.citation: Oxford Nanopore Technologies, modkit (github.com/nanoporetech/modkit); DMR docs nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/intro_dmr.html + dmr_scoring_details.html.

tools.name: pycoMeth Meth_Comp (MetH5 read-groups)
tools.what_it_does: Toolbox for differential methylation from ONT calls built on the MetH5 storage format. CpG_Aggregate or Interval_Aggregate produce per-CpG / per-interval methylation; Meth_Comp compares n samples OR n haplotypes (if haplotype is stored as read-groups in MetH5) to call ASM within a single sample.
tools.statistic: Per-CpG or per-interval beta values compared with a NON-PARAMETRIC test: MANN-WHITNEY U for 2 groups (= HP1 vs HP2), KRUSKAL-WALLIS for >2 groups; p-values BH-FDR adjusted; supports independent hypothesis weighting (IHW). Hypothesis modes bs_diff / llr_diff / count_dependency. Region calls via multi-sample consensus segmentation (Meth_Seg).
tools.granularity: Both: per-CpG position and per-interval (segment) aggregation.
tools.cancer_or_germline: Generic; haplotype read-groups -> single-sample ASM (germline allelic axis). No built-in somatic/imprinting subtraction.
tools.citation: Snajder R. et al., 'pycoMeth: a toolbox for differential methylation testing from Nanopore methylation calls', Genome Biology 2023;24:83. DOI 10.1186/s13059-023-02917-w.

tools.name: O'Neill / POG long-read cancer cohort pipeline (Cell Genomics 2024)
tools.what_it_does: Canonical CANCER cohort instantiation of AXIS 1: 189 tumors + 41 matched normals, ONT PromethION. Long-range phasing -> haplotagged reads -> per-haplotype methylation -> genome-wide aDMR discovery; finds recurrent allelic DMRs at cancer-gene promoters (RET, CDKN2A) and clinically actionable promoter methylation (MLH1, BRCA1, RAD51C).
tools.statistic: aDMR call = DSS (beta-binomial Wald, as in NanoMethPhase) on per-haplotype methylation with a thresholded effect: average allele-specific methylation must differ by >= 0.1 (|Delta-beta| >= 0.1) between alleles. Phasing = WhatsHap (bundled with Clair3) for SNVs; methylation phasing = NanoMethPhase 1.2.0. SOMATIC specificity obtained by EXCLUDING aDMRs attributable to imprinting or random/constitutive allele-specific methylation (normal-cell ASM filtered out).
tools.granularity: Region (promoter/enhancer/polyA-anchored aDMRs); 2,854 genes / 8,511 transcripts with recurrent promoter aDMRs.
tools.cancer_or_germline: CANCER somatic, but the core HP1-vs-HP2 engine is germline-allelic; somatic isolation is post-hoc imprinting/normal exclusion, NOT a within-engine somatic-controlled axis.
tools.citation: O'Neill K. et al., 'Long-read sequencing of an advanced cancer cohort resolves rearrangements, unravels haplotypes, and reveals methylation landscapes', Cell Genomics 2024;4(11):100674. DOI 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100674. PMC11605692.

tools.name: NANOME (Nextflow, LabShengLi)
tools.what_it_does: Haplotype-aware Nextflow pipeline producing a CONSENSUS per-read 5mC call (XGBoost over Megalodon + Nanopolish + DeepSignal), then combines variant calling + longphase phasing to detect allele-specific methylation; supports 5mC/5hmC and T2T genome; benchmarked on imprinting controls.
tools.statistic: Consensus methylation = XGBoost meta-model over 3 callers (improves single-base precision ~11%, single-molecule accuracy ~2.4%; ~200k extra CpGs). Haplotype ASM/DMR called downstream on the phased consensus calls (region DMR density compared gap vs non-gap on T2T); the ASM significance step reuses standard per-CpG/region DMR testing on the consensus bedMethyl rather than introducing a new test.
tools.granularity: Per-CpG consensus call; region DMR downstream.
tools.cancer_or_germline: Generic / germline allelic (validated on known imprinting controls); not cancer-somatic specific.
tools.citation: NANOME, bioRxiv 2025 DOI 10.1101/2025.06.29.662079; PubMed 40631091; github.com/LabShengLi/nanome.

tools.name: longphase modcall / co-phasing + WhatsHap haplotag (phasing+haplotag backbone)
tools.what_it_does: Upstream backbone shared by every AXIS-1 pipeline: produces the phased VCF and HP-tagged BAM all downstream per-haplotype methylation tools consume. longphase co-phases SNP/indel/SV/5mC chromosome-scale in minutes (modcall emits per-site 5mC VCF); whatshap haplotag / longphase haplotag write HP:Z tags. Not a DMR caller itself.
tools.statistic: No DMR statistic of its own; provides the HP partition + phase-set (PS). Phasing quality measured by switch-error / block N50; readConfidence threshold (longphase default 0.65) governs which reads receive an HP tag.
tools.granularity: Read-level HP tag + per-site phased 5mC (modcall VCF).
tools.cancer_or_germline: Germline phasing (longphase) / somatic variants (longphase-S/-TO add somatic + LOH); haplotag axis germline by construction.
tools.citation: Lin J-H. et al., 'LongPhase: an ultra-fast chromosome-scale phasing algorithm', GigaScience 2022;11:giac104 (DOI 10.1093/gigascience/giac104). WhatsHap: Martin M. et al., bioRxiv 2016 DOI 10.1101/085050.

difficulties: PHASING DEPENDENCE (root weakness): the whole axis is downstream of correctly phased germline het SNVs. No/few het SNVs in a window -> no haplotype block -> reads stay untagged -> methylation cannot be partitioned. Phasing switch-errors silently swap HP1/HP2 methylation, faking or destroying aDMRs. Block N50 caps how far apart two CpGs can be co-attributed to the same allele.

LOH DESTROYS HET ANCHORS (cancer-specific, severe): tumor copy-number LOH deletes one allele's heterozygous SNVs, so exactly the regions most interesting in cancer (deleted tumor suppressors, e.g. CDKN2A) have the FEWEST anchors to phase -> haplotagging fails precisely where you want ASM. cnLOH also makes both 'haplotypes' derive from one parental allele, so HP1-vs-HP2 no longer means two distinct alleles.

HP1-vs-HP2 IS A GERMLINE AXIS, NOT A SOMATIC ONE (the conceptual ceiling): comparing the two germline haplotypes mixes constitutive imprinting, random monoallelic methylation, and true somatic events. A significant HP1!=HP2 difference does NOT tell you it is tumor-acquired. The field handles this only by POST-HOC exclusion of imprinted/known-ASM loci using a matched normal (POG), which discards signal and cannot catch tumor-specific changes that land on an imprinted locus. There is no within-engine 'somatic-on-HP1' (HP1 vs HP1-mutated) axis.

GERMLINE IMPRINTING CONFOUND: hundreds of imprinted DMRs are constitutively allele-specific; without a normal control they dominate the aDMR list and masquerade as cancer ASM. Requires curated imprinting blacklists or matched-normal subtraction.

COVERAGE PER HAPLOTYPE (power halves): splitting reads into HP1/HP2 halves depth per pile; a CpG needing ~10x now needs ~20x to phase confidently. DSS/modkit tests lose power; low-depth CpGs are dropped or give unstable beta. In low-purity/low-coverage tumors many CpGs fall below the min-coverage gate.

TUMOR PURITY / ADMIXTURE: normal-cell contamination dilutes tumor methylation toward 50/50, shrinking Delta-beta below the |0.1| call threshold; a real somatic ASM in a 30%-pure sample can be invisible. Purity also distorts the allelic balance used for phasing.

SINGLE-SAMPLE STATISTICAL POWER: per-tumor ASM is one observation; the per-CpG tests (Wald / Mann-Whitney) treat read counts as replicates = pseudo-replication at the patient level. Cohort recurrence (POG's 189) is what gives confidence; a single cancer sample yields weak, hard-to-calibrate p-values.

HETEROGENEITY / EPIPOLYMORPHISM: a tumor is a mix of subclones; a CpG can read 50% methylated because half the cells are fully methylated, not because the allele is hemi-methylated. Per-haplotype MEAN methylation collapses read-to-read structure and cannot distinguish bimodal subclonal methylation from uniform intermediate methylation -- the axis sees a beta, not a distribution.

COPY-NUMBER skews per-haplotype read counts (amplified allele contributes more reads), biasing the beta estimate and the binomial/beta-binomial variance; uncorrected CN inflates or deflates Delta-beta.

5mC vs 5hmC COLLAPSE: many pipelines (and any 2-state Beta-Binomial) lump 5mC+5hmC or model only 5mC; in ONT modBAM the MM/ML tags carry both, so a 'methylation difference' can be a 5mC<->5hmC swap, not true hypo/hyper change (modkit's Dirichlet-Multinomial mode mitigates; DSS/NanoMethPhase 2-state does not).

REGION-DEFINITION ARBITRARINESS: DMR boundaries depend on smoothing bandwidth (DSS) or HMM segmentation params (modkit --segment); the same data yields different aDMR counts under different settings, and the |Delta-beta|>=0.1 + min-CpG gate is a heuristic, not a calibrated test.
axes.ism_difference: AXIS 1 (industry) and ISM differ on THREE structural points. (1) UNIT OF COMPARISON: AXIS 1 collapses each haplotype to a per-CpG MEAN beta and tests HP1-mean vs HP2-mean (DSS Wald / modkit LR / pycoMeth Mann-Whitney). ISM keeps the full read x CpG matrix and builds an explicit read-to-read NHD distance matrix -> UPGMA + silhouette -> PERMANOVA pseudo-F structure test (+ dispersion + LabelTest delta = d_between - d_within). ISM therefore tests whether reads form distinct epigenetic GROUPS (subclonal structure / epipolymorphism), which the mean-collapse of AXIS 1 is blind to -- directly addressing the heterogeneity/epipolymorphism pain-point above. (2) THE AXIS BEING COMPARED: AXIS 1's HP1-vs-HP2 is intrinsically a GERMLINE allelic axis, with somatic specificity handled only by post-hoc imprinting exclusion against a normal. ISM consumes LOH-constrained phasing tags (HP1 germline / HP1-1 somatic-on-HP1 / HP2 / HP2-1) and runs a SOMATIC-CONTROLLED HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis (same parental haplotype, with vs without the somatic event) -- a within-engine somatic contrast AXIS 1 structurally lacks. ISM also adds a normal-anchored cis-test (normal-HP1 baseline; d_cis vs d_drift) to separate true somatic cis-effects from germline drift and copy-number, the exact confound AXIS 1 can only filter, not measure. (3) PURPOSE / HONESTY: AXIS 1 is built to CALL aDMRs (a discovery/characterization claim). ISM mirrors AXIS 1 at its site level (per-CpG Fisher exact + BH-FDR, Cramer's V with a Cochran min-expected-count gate, Delta-beta Wilcoxon + Cohen's d on the HP1-vs-HP1-1 somatic axis), so it can reproduce the canonical statistic -- but ISM explicitly tested methylation as a TP/FP somatic-variant FILTER and found it NEGATIVE four independent ways: ASM is real but NOT discriminative, positioning ISM as characterization, not a filter. POSITIONING: ISM is downstream of the AXIS-1 phasing/haplotag backbone (longphase-TO/-S LOH-constrained tags) and substitutes a read-distance + PERMANOVA structure engine and a somatic-controlled HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis (+ normal-anchored cis-test) for AXIS 1's per-haplotype mean-collapse and germline HP1-vs-HP2 DMR call; ISM's Fisher / Cramer's-V / Delta-beta site layer is its AXIS-1-equivalent secondary view rather than the headline result.

axes.axis: AXIS 2 — Read-level methylation distance / clustering (read-to-read structure from per-read CpG methylation vectors)
axes.canonical_workflow: Standard pipeline on this axis: (1) Acquire per-read methylation calls — for ONT long reads from MM/ML BAM tags (5mC/5hmC), for legacy data from bisulfite alignments — and build a read × CpG matrix over a window/region, with entries methylated(1)/unmethylated(0)/missing(-1). (2) Choose a between-read comparison: either (a) explicit read-to-read distance (normalized Hamming / NHD over co-covered CpGs, the FDRP/qFDRP/MeConcord/ISM family) then cluster (hierarchical/UPGMA, density-based HDBSCAN, or k-medoids), or (b) model-based latent clustering that skips the distance matrix (multivariate-Bernoulli mixture fit by EM — cvlr/ASMS), typically K=2 for two epialleles. (3) Decide how many subpopulations exist and whether the split is real (silhouette / best-likelihood seed / model selection). (4) Test structure significance — most legacy WSH tools STOP at a per-CpG score and have NO native between-group test; the long-read engines add either a permutation/PERMANOVA structure test (ISM), a binomial test vs a mean-methylation null (MeConcord), an empirical permutation p-value + Fisher haplotype-enrichment (cvlr), or a cluster-vs-SNP concordance p-value (ASMS). (5) For cancer somatic work, separate biologically meaningful subclonal/allelic structure from confounds (germline ASM/imprinting, copy number, tumor purity, epipolymorphic noise) — this final disambiguation step is essentially absent from every surveyed tool and is where ISM's normal-anchored cis-test sits.

tools.name: ISM (InterSubMod) — ours
tools.what_it_does: Builds an EXPLICIT read-to-read NHD distance matrix from the read×CpG matrix (5mC+5hmC from MM/ML), then UPGMA + silhouette to call subclonal read groups; this read-distance engine is the PRIMARY engine. Pairs it with a site-level axis (per-CpG Fisher exact + BH-FDR, Cramer V + Cochran gate, Delta-beta Wilcoxon + Cohen d) and a tag-compare axis consuming LOH-constrained phasing HP tags (somatic-controlled HP1-vs-HP1-1, not just HP1-vs-HP2).
tools.statistic: Read-distance: NHD pairwise distance -> UPGMA + silhouette; PERMANOVA pseudo-F with permutation p-value (structure test) + dispersion test + LabelTest delta = d_between - d_within. Unique: normal-anchored cis-test (normal-HP1 baseline; d_cis vs d_drift) to separate somatic cis from germline drift + copy number.
tools.citation: Internal method (this project); src/core/DistanceMatrix.cpp, HierarchicalClustering.cpp, StructureTest.cpp, LabelTest.cpp, PerCpgAsm.cpp
tools.cancer_or_germline: cancer somatic (LOH-constrained phasing; somatic HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis); normal-anchored cis-test for germline-vs-somatic disambiguation

tools.name: cvlr
tools.what_it_does: Finds heterogeneously methylated genomic regions from ONT reads WITHOUT a prior phasing step. Represents data as a binary read×position matrix (0/1/-1) and clusters reads directly into K groups via a mixture of multivariate Bernoulli distributions; captures allele-specific differences AND other heterogeneity (cell subpopulations). Three executables: cvlr-cluster, cvlr-meth-of-bam, cvlr-stats.
tools.statistic: Multivariate-Bernoulli mixture model fit by Expectation-Maximization (Dempster 1977); does NOT build a read-to-read distance matrix (model-based latent clustering instead). K user-specified (K=2 in paper examples), not auto-selected; multiple random-seed restarts, pick best likelihood. Significance: empirical permutation p-value from 1000 random cluster assignments + Fisher exact test for haplotype enrichment per cluster. No BIC/AIC/LRT model-selection criterion for K.
tools.citation: Raineri et al. 2023, Bioinformatics Advances 3(1):vbac101. DOI: 10.1093/bioadv/vbac101 ; PMID 36698762 ; https://github.com/EmanueleRaineri/cvlr
tools.granularity: read-clustering (model-based, no explicit distance matrix); region/window level
tools.cancer_or_germline: germline/general heterogeneity (phasing-free; not cancer-somatic-specific)

tools.name: ASMS (Raineri 2024)
tools.what_it_does: Detects allele-specific methylation in human genomes WITHOUT a prior phasing step; extends the cvlr idea to a genome-wide ASM scan. asms cluster subdivides long reads into 2 groups by methylation content; cluster-by-snp tests the split against SNPs. Designed to find ASM/heterogeneity where no other no-phasing method exists (contrast hap-ASM, Methphaser, modkit which require phasing).
tools.statistic: Bernoulli-mixture EM with EXACTLY 2 clusters (not configurable; --maxit default 10, --seed). Generates per-region methylation matrices (outdir/matrices/) but no read-to-read distance matrix. Significance: cluster-by-snp subcommand outputs p-values + adjusted p-values for ASM (concordance of EM clusters with SNP alleles); asm.bed (BED9) reports putative ASM regions with cluster sizes + median methylation. Targets intermediate-methylation regions (default beta bounds ~0.4-0.6).
tools.citation: Raineri et al. 2024, bioRxiv (PREPRINT, not peer-reviewed). DOI: 10.1101/2024.12.18.629129 ; https://github.com/ecmra/asms
tools.granularity: read-clustering (model-based, no explicit distance matrix); genome-wide region level
tools.cancer_or_germline: germline ASM focus (phasing-free); not cancer-somatic-validated

tools.name: modbamtools cluster (HDBSCAN)
tools.what_it_does: Visualization + analysis of single-molecule base-modification data from long-read BAM (ONT/PacBio). Single-molecule plots = one read per horizontal bar (methylated red / unmethylated blue). cluster command (or --cluster in plotting) groups reads by per-read modification state over bed-file regions to quantify cell types / early-cancer heterogeneity.
tools.statistic: HDBSCAN (Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise; McInnes JOSS DOI 10.21105/joss.00205) on per-read methylation feature vectors. No native read-to-read distance matrix is exposed and NO significance/statistical test — clustering is exploratory / for visualization and heterogeneity profiling, not hypothesis testing.
tools.citation: Razaghi, Hook et al. 2022, bioRxiv. DOI: 10.1101/2022.07.07.499188 ; https://github.com/rrazaghi/modbamtools ; docs https://rrazaghi.github.io/modbamtools/
tools.cancer_or_germline: general/heterogeneity + early cancer detection (no somatic-specific test)

tools.name: qFDRP / FDRP (Scherer 2020, WSH)
tools.what_it_does: Within-sample heterogeneity (WSH) scores at single-CpG resolution computed from PAIRS of reads covering a target CpG. FDRP = fraction of discordant read pairs (a pair is discordant if any co-covered CpG differs); qFDRP = soft/quantitative version using the normalized Hamming distance averaged over read pairs (less sensitive to single-CpG fluctuations & CpG density).
tools.statistic: Read-PAIR comparison (read-to-read at the pair level, not a stored full matrix). FDRP = discordant-pair fraction; qFDRP = mean normalized Hamming distance over read pairs covering the CpG. NO built-in significance test — these are per-CpG scores; downstream testing = transform to M-values + limma + Benjamini-Hochberg to call DMRs/DHRs. Combinatorial O(N^2)-in-coverage cost forces subsampling (randomly sample 40 reads when coverage >40); min overlap 35bp, 50bp window, min coverage ~10x.
tools.citation: Scherer et al. 2020, Nucleic Acids Research 48(8):e46. DOI: 10.1093/nar/gkaa120 ; PMID 32103242 ; R pkg MPIIComputationalEpigenetics/WSHPackage
tools.platform: bisulfite short reads (WGBS/RRBS) by design; applied per-CpG
tools.granularity: read-PAIR -> per-CpG WSH score (no clustering, no full distance matrix)
tools.cancer_or_germline: general heterogeneity (captures ASM/cell-type/contamination); no somatic vs germline separation

tools.name: MeConcord
tools.what_it_does: Quantifies local methylation concordance across reads AND across CpG sites within 150bp bins. Reads-concordance (RC) measures agreement between read pairs; CpGs-concordance (CC) measures agreement between site pairs. Normalized versions subtract the concordance expected from mean methylation, so the score reflects structure beyond bulk methylation level.
tools.statistic: Hamming-distance pairwise comparison implemented via matrix multiplication (3 binary matrices M/N/T) — does NOT store an explicit read-to-read distance matrix. RC/CC -> Normalized RC/CC = observed minus expected (expected from mean-methylation null). Significance: BINOMIAL test p-values (cumulative binomial) against the mean-methylation null. Window 150bp, >5 CpGs/bin; handles >1000 reads/bin (much higher capacity than FDRP's ~40x).
tools.citation: Wang lab 2022, Bioinformatics 38(Suppl 1):i307-i315. DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac248 ; PMID 35758820 ; https://github.com/WangLabTHU/MeConcord
tools.granularity: read-read + CpG-CpG concordance -> per-bin score + binomial p (no read clustering)
tools.cancer_or_germline: general heterogeneity (imprinting/CTCF shown); no somatic-vs-germline separation

tools.name: Metheor (CLARIFY: within-read, NOT read-to-read)
tools.what_it_does: Ultrafast Rust tool computing intra-/inter-cellular methylation heterogeneity measures via a one-sweep algorithm that scans each read ONCE. CLARIFICATION: it is WITHIN-read heterogeneity, NOT a read-to-read distance/clustering engine — it does not build a read×read matrix and does not cluster reads. Treats methylation states co-occurring on one read as pseudo-barcodes.
tools.statistic: Computes PDR (proportion of discordant reads), epipolymorphism, methylation entropy, MHL, FDRP, qFDRP, and the novel LPMD (Local Pairwise Methylation Discordance = discordance between two CpGs at fixed distance ON THE SAME read, read-length-invariant). NO native significance test (downstream Pearson + BH, t-tests in paper). One-sweep O(reads), 13.7-175.8x faster than WSHPackage.
tools.citation: Lee et al. 2023, PLOS Computational Biology 19(3):e1010946. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010946 ; PMID 36976832 ; https://github.com/dohlee/metheor
tools.platform: bisulfite short reads (25-50bp focus, RRBS); no long-read mode described
tools.granularity: WITHIN-read discordance scores (per-region); NOT read-to-read, NOT clustering
tools.cancer_or_germline: general heterogeneity; no somatic-vs-germline separation

difficulties: NO native significance test in most tools: qFDRP/FDRP, MeConcord (per-CpG/per-bin scores), Metheor, and modbamtools (exploratory HDBSCAN) emit a score or a partition but do NOT test 'is there real read-level structure here?'. Only cvlr (permutation p + Fisher), ASMS (cluster-vs-SNP p), MeConcord (binomial vs mean-methylation null), and ISM (PERMANOVA pseudo-F permutation) provide a structure/between-group test. Without one, calling a region 'heterogeneous' is a thresholded score, easily inflated.

Coverage / power: every read-pair or read-clustering method degrades at low depth. ONT cancer BAMs vary widely; FDRP needs subsampling above ~40x and is unstable below ~10x; cvlr/ASMS EM mixtures need enough reads per latent cluster to estimate per-CpG Bernoulli parameters; a 2-cluster fit on thin coverage hallucinates structure. Tumor purity dilutes the somatic subpopulation, further cutting effective depth.

Distance-metric choice is non-trivial and consequential: normalized Hamming / NHD over only CO-COVERED CpGs is the default, but missing data (-1), unequal overlap length, CpG density, and read length all bias the distance (FDRP rises with read length & CpG density; qFDRP and LPMD were explicitly invented to fix this). The metric choice silently determines which reads look 'close'.

Compute scales badly: explicit read-to-read distance is O(N^2) pairs and clustering can be O(N^2) (UPGMA) to O(N^3); read-pair WSH is combinatorial in coverage (hence forced subsampling, which then makes results non-reproducible across runs). Model-based EM (cvlr/ASMS) sidesteps the matrix but adds seed-dependence (must restart and pick best likelihood) and a fixed/unselected K.

What the distance/cluster MEANS biologically is ambiguous: a read-level split can be allele (germline ASM/imprinting), cell-subpopulation/subclone, copy-number-driven (extra alleles inflate apparent groups), or just epipolymorphic stochastic noise. The phasing-free tools (cvlr/ASMS/modbamtools) deliberately conflate all of these ('captures ASM AND other heterogeneity'), so a positive call is NOT automatically a somatic subclonal signal.

Germline-vs-somatic confound (cancer-specific): none of the 7 surveyed tools natively separates a SOMATIC cis-acting methylation difference from a pre-existing GERMLINE allelic/imprinted difference or copy-number-driven drift. ASMS even targets germline ASM by design. In cancer this is the central trap — the read split may be 100% germline/imprinting and 0% tumor.

Single-sample power & no replication: read-level heterogeneity is typically called per-sample with no biological replicate, so a permutation/binomial p-value tests structure-vs-shuffle WITHIN one sample but cannot establish reproducibility across tumors or rule out sample-specific artifacts.

Phasing dependence cuts both ways: phasing-free tools (cvlr/ASMS/modbamtools) avoid needing HP tags but lose the ability to anchor a split to a specific somatic-vs-germline allele; tag-consuming approaches (ISM) gain that control but inherit all errors and coverage limits of the upstream (LOH-constrained) phasing.

Bisulfite-era heritage: FDRP/qFDRP, MeConcord, and Metheor were built and benchmarked on short bisulfite reads (35-150bp windows, CpG-only, no 5hmC). Applying them to ONT long reads with 5mC+5hmC and read-spanning multi-kb windows is off-design — long reads break the read-length-invariance assumptions (PDR/FDRP read-length bias) and 5mC/5hmC must be collapsed or handled explicitly.
axes.ism_difference: ISM is the only surveyed approach that combines all four of: (1) an EXPLICIT read-to-read NHD distance matrix as the primary engine (cvlr/ASMS skip the matrix with model-based EM; Metheor is within-read only; FDRP/MeConcord do pairwise reads but never store/cluster a full matrix), (2) UPGMA + silhouette to call subclonal groups, (3) a genuine between-group STRUCTURE test (PERMANOVA pseudo-F with permutation + dispersion + LabelTest delta) where most peers stop at a score, and (4) a cancer-specific confound control via the normal-anchored cis-test (normal-HP1 baseline; d_cis vs d_drift) plus somatic-controlled HP1-vs-HP1-1 tag axis. The peer tools' headline strength — phasing-free heterogeneity detection (cvlr/ASMS) — is precisely what makes them unable to tell somatic-cis from germline/imprinting/copy-number, the exact disambiguation ISM targets. ISM's documented honest limitation is that the read-level methylation signal, while real (ASM exists), is NOT a usable TP/FP somatic variant filter (NEGATIVE four ways) — it is a characterization engine, not a discriminator, and it depends on upstream LOH-constrained phasing quality.
axes.where_ism_sits: ISM sits at the structure-testing + somatic-disambiguation end of AXIS 2: it occupies the explicit-distance-matrix + clustering + PERMANOVA niche (closest in spirit to cvlr/ASMS read-clustering, but with a stored distance matrix, a real structure test, and cancer-specific confound controls the phasing-free tools lack), while treating the WSH score family (qFDRP/FDRP/MeConcord/Metheor) as descriptive heterogeneity scores rather than read-clustering engines.

axes.axis: AXIS 3 — Site-level / region-level methylation difference detection (per-CpG DMP + DMR calling); the explicit-statistic axis answering "WHICH positions/regions differ in mean methylation between two groups (e.g. tumor-vs-normal, HP1-vs-HP1-1), and by how much."
axes.canonical_workflow: Standard DMR/DMP pipeline: (1) Build a per-CpG count matrix (methylated reads m, total reads n) per sample/group from BS-seq or ONT MM/ML calls. (2) Optionally SMOOTH methylation estimates along the genome (BSmooth local-likelihood, DSS pseudo-replicate smoothing, DMRcate Gaussian kernel) to borrow strength across neighboring CpGs and stabilize low-coverage sites. (3) Per-CpG TEST for differential methylation under a count model: beta-binomial Wald (DSS), logistic/Fisher (methylKit), beta-binomial credible-difference (MOABS), limma moderated-t on M-values (DMRcate), binomial-Beta marginal-likelihood (modkit). (4) Correct genome-wide MULTIPLE TESTING (BH-FDR or q-value/SLIM) at the DMP level. (5) AGGREGATE adjacent significant/concordant CpGs into REGIONS while handling spatial autocorrelation: segmentation (metilene CBS), region-statistic + permutation null (dmrseq, DMRcate-Satterthwaite), or p-value combination (comb-p Stouffer-Liptak + Sidak). (6) Report each DMR with an EFFECT SIZE (mean delta-beta, Cohen's d or h, CDIF) plus region-level FDR, then rank/threshold. Output is a ranked DMR table (chr,start,end,nCpG,delta-beta,stat,FDR). In ONT cancer somatic use, this is run tumor-vs-matched-normal or, in ISM's framing, on a somatic-controlled haplotype axis.

tools.name: DSS (Feng/Conneely/Wu 2014 single-CpG; Park & Wu 2016 general design)
tools.what_it_does: Beta-binomial model for BS-seq counts. 2014 version: Bayesian hierarchical model with a log-normal prior on dispersion phi, dispersion shrunk genome-wide (empirical Bayes); SPATIAL handling = neighboring CpGs treated as 'pseudo-replicates' via a smoothing window so per-site variance is stabilized at low coverage. 2016 'DSS-general': beta-binomial regression with arcsine link, fit by GLS, supports arbitrary multi-factor designs; this version explicitly does NOT model spatial correlation in the test (acknowledged limitation). callDMR() merges adjacent significant CpGs by distance/proportion thresholds.
tools.statistic: Wald test on beta-binomial regression coefficient: t = C^T beta-hat / sqrt(C^T Sigma-hat C); var(Z_id) ~ 1 + (m_id-1)phi_i/m_id; dispersion via empirical-Bayes log-normal-prior shrinkage (2014) or Pearson-chi2 GLS estimate bounded [0.001,0.999] (2016); BH-FDR. Granularity per-CpG (DMP) + region (callDMR). Platform BS-seq/WGBS/RRBS counts.
tools.citation: Feng H, Conneely KN, Wu H. Nucleic Acids Res 2014;42(8):e69, DOI 10.1093/nar/gku154. Park Y, Wu H. Bioinformatics 2016;32(10):1446-1453, DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btw026.
tools.platform: BS-seq / WGBS / RRBS (count-based; applicable to ONT per-CpG pileups)
tools.cancer_or_germline: general two-group / multifactor; widely used tumor-vs-normal

tools.name: methylKit
tools.what_it_does: Per-base/per-region differential methylation by either Fisher's exact test (no replicates) or logistic regression comparing fraction methylated across groups, with optional overdispersion correction. SPATIAL handling = none in the test (adjacent CpGs independent); spatial structure only via user-defined tiling windows.
tools.statistic: Logistic regression on (methylated, unmethylated) counts with group covariate, OR Fisher's exact test; overdispersion correction 'MN' (McCullagh-Nelder variance scaling) or 'shrinkMN' (scaling shrunk to common value); multiple testing via SLIM q-value (default) or BH. Granularity per-CpG/per-base (DMC) or tiled windows.
tools.citation: Akalin A, Kormaksson M, Li S, et al. Genome Biology 2012;13(10):R87, DOI 10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r87.
tools.platform: BS-seq / RRBS / WGBS (count-based; usable on ONT per-CpG counts)
tools.cancer_or_germline: general two-group; common in cancer cohort studies

tools.name: metilene
tools.what_it_does: De-novo DMR caller via fast circular binary segmentation (CBS) directly on the mean methylation-difference signal between two groups, then statistical testing of candidate segments. No prior region annotation needed. SPATIAL handling = intrinsic, since CBS segments contiguous CpGs so the region is the unit of analysis.
tools.statistic: Circular binary segmentation maximizing mean methylation difference; segmentation termination via 2D Kolmogorov-Smirnov (2D-KS) test p-value (jointly position+methylation); final DMRs tested with Mann-Whitney U test (and 2D-KS p-value), multiple-testing adjusted; effect size = mean methylation difference. Can run with as few as one sample per group (handles/estimates missing data).
tools.citation: Juhling F, Kretzmer H, Bernhart SH, et al. Genome Research 2016;26(2):256-262, DOI 10.1101/gr.196394.115, PMID 26631489.
tools.cancer_or_germline: general two-group; works with single sample per group

tools.name: bsseq / BSmooth
tools.what_it_does: Local-likelihood smoothing of WGBS methylation to get reliable semi-local estimates at variable/low coverage, then a smoothed signal-to-noise t-statistic between groups to call DMRs by thresholding. SPATIAL handling = core feature (genome-position smoothing borrows information across neighboring CpGs), but the t-statistic has no parametric null so significance is heuristic.
tools.statistic: Local likelihood regression (coverage-weighted kernel, fitted parabola) for a smooth methylation curve; group t-statistic = (mean1-mean2)/smoothed-SE, where the SD estimate is itself smoothed (running mean width k) and floored at the qSd quantile; NO known null distribution (user picks |t| cutoff). Requires total samples >=3.
tools.citation: Hansen KD, Langmead B, Irizarry RA. Genome Biology 2012;13(10):R83, DOI 10.1186/gb-2012-13-10-r83, PMID 23034175.
tools.cancer_or_germline: general; foundational for cancer WGBS DMR work

tools.name: dmrseq
tools.what_it_does: Region-level inference with genome-wide-comparable statistics and rigorous FDR via permutation, designed for as few as two samples per group. SPATIAL handling = explicit AR(1) autoregressive error structure modeling inter-CpG correlation within regions; permutation null makes region statistics comparable across the genome.
tools.statistic: Region statistic from a generalized least squares (GLS) regression on transformed methylation proportions with a nested autoregressive AR(1) correlated-error structure (models inter-individual AND inter-CpG variability); region score (coefficient/area) compared to a POOLED PERMUTATION null distribution to control genome-wide FDR; effect size = GLS beta coefficient.
tools.citation: Korthauer K, Chakraborty S, Benjamini Y, Irizarry RA. Biostatistics 2018;19(3):367-383, DOI 10.1093/biostatistics/kxy007 (preprint DOI 10.1101/183210).
tools.cancer_or_germline: general two-group; >=2 samples/group

tools.name: DMRcate
tools.what_it_does: Kernel-smoothing DMR caller: per-CpG limma differential statistics are spatially smoothed with a Gaussian kernel, and significance of the smoothed signal is tested against a null. Originally 450K/EPIC array, extended to WGBS. SPATIAL handling = explicit Gaussian-kernel smoothing over genomic distance with CpG-density correction; Satterthwaite df accounts for the smoothing.
tools.statistic: Square of limma moderated t-statistic per CpG -> Gaussian-kernel-weighted smoothing within bandwidth; two smoothed estimates (t-weighted vs null) compared via Satterthwaite approximation for a region p-value; effect size = mean beta/M-value difference (maxdiff/meandiff); BH-FDR.
tools.citation: Peters TJ, Buckley MJ, Statham AL, et al. Epigenetics & Chromatin 2015;8:6, DOI 10.1186/1756-8935-8-6, PMID 25972926. WGBS extension: Peters TJ et al. Nucleic Acids Res 2021;49(19):e109, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkab637.
tools.cancer_or_germline: general; heavily used in cancer array cohorts

tools.name: comb-p
tools.what_it_does: Post-hoc, method-agnostic region builder that takes per-CpG p-values from ANY upstream test (BED of p-values), accounts for spatial autocorrelation, combines adjacent p-values, and assigns region-level FDR-corrected significance. SPATIAL handling = explicit and central: empirically estimated autocorrelation (ACF) at each lag weights the p-value combination.
tools.statistic: Stouffer-Liptak: p-values -> Z-scores, summed/scaled into a combined Z, with neighbors weighted by the observed autocorrelation at the relevant lag; regions seeded by sliding-window combined p; 1-step Sidak correction on the region p-value based on number of possible regions of that size; then BH.
tools.citation: Pedersen BS, Schwartz DA, Yang IV, Kechris KJ. Bioinformatics 2012;28(22):2986-2988, DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/bts545, PMID 22954632.
tools.platform: platform-agnostic (consumes p-values from array, BS-seq, or ONT upstream tests)
tools.cancer_or_germline: general; common in EWAS / cancer methylome studies

tools.name: MOABS
tools.what_it_does: Model-based BS-seq DM detection at single-CpG resolution using a beta-binomial hierarchical model, reporting a single credible-difference metric (CDIF) that unifies biological magnitude and statistical confidence; strong at low (5-10x) coverage. SPATIAL handling = none in the core CDIF test (single-CpG); regions formed by merging, not by a spatial-correlation model.
tools.statistic: Beta-binomial hierarchical model: methylated reads ~ Binomial given ratio, ratio ~ Beta (captures sampling + biological variation); CDIF = credible methylation difference = the boundary of the 95% credible interval of the methylation difference nearest to 0 (lower bound when CI excludes 0) -- a depth-aware shrunken effect size, NOT a raw delta-beta.
tools.citation: Sun D, Xi Y, Rodriguez B, et al. Genome Biology 2014;15(2):R38, DOI 10.1186/gb-2014-15-2-r38, PMID 24565500.
tools.cancer_or_germline: general two-group; designed for/benefits low-coverage cancer WGBS

tools.name: modkit dmr (Oxford Nanopore)
tools.what_it_does: ONT-native differential methylation scorer operating directly on modkit pileups (5mC etc.). 'dmr pair' scores supplied regions or single bases between two samples; the ONLY tool here purpose-built for long-read modified-base calls. SPATIAL handling = region score aggregates all bases in the supplied interval into one marginal likelihood (region is the unit) but no explicit autocorrelation/AR model; regions must be provided (no de-novo segmentation).
tools.statistic: Region score = log marginal likelihood ratio log[ l_theta_a(Xa) * l_theta_b(Xb) / l_theta_ab(Xa+b) ] under a Binomial likelihood with conjugate Beta (Jeffreys / Beta(0.5,0.5)) prior (separate-vs-pooled fit). Single-base mode adds a MAP-based p-value pMAP = f(0)/f(d) with d = phat1 - phat2. Region effect size reported as Cohen's h (used instead of MAP p-value for regions because MAP destabilizes at high coverage). Balanced replicates enable paired effect sizes / MAP p-values.
tools.citation: Oxford Nanopore Technologies modkit docs: 'DMR model and scoring details' (software-docs.nanoporetech.com/modkit/dmr_scoring_details.html) and 'Perform differential methylation scoring' (nanoporetech.github.io/modkit/intro_dmr.html); repo github.com/nanoporetech/modkit.
tools.platform: ONT long-read modified-base pileups (modkit) -- directly relevant to ISM context
tools.granularity: region (dmr pair, supplied intervals) + single-base (likelihood-ratio + MAP p-value)
tools.cancer_or_germline: general two-sample contrast (e.g. tumor-vs-normal); single-sample weaker than replicated/paired

difficulties: OVER-DISPERSION: read counts at a CpG are NOT simple binomial -- biological + technical variance inflates variance, so a plain Fisher/binomial test is anticonservative. Every credible tool (DSS, MOABS, methylKit-MN, dmrseq) must model dispersion (beta-binomial) or scale variance, and dispersion is hard to estimate per-site at low coverage (hence empirical-Bayes shrinkage). In ONT cancer somatic this is worse: subclonal mixtures create real per-read heterogeneity that masquerades as over-dispersion.

GENOME-WIDE MULTIPLE TESTING: ~28M CpGs in human -> millions of correlated tests. BH-FDR assumes independence/PRDS that adjacent CpGs violate; q-value (methylKit SLIM), permutation null (dmrseq), and Sidak-on-possible-regions (comb-p) are different attempts to control region-level FDR honestly. Over-merging or window choice silently changes the effective number of tests.

SPATIAL CpG AUTOCORRELATION: neighboring CpGs are co-methylated, so per-site p-values are not independent -- naive region calling double-counts evidence and inflates significance. Tools diverge sharply (dmrseq AR(1), comb-p ACF-weighted Stouffer-Liptak, DMRcate Gaussian kernel, metilene CBS) and produce DIFFERENT region boundaries from the same data; there is no consensus 'true' DMR set.

COVERAGE / LOW-DEPTH: methylation estimate variance scales with 1/n; at 5-10x (typical WGBS / ONT tumor) per-site beta is noisy. Smoothing (BSmooth, DSS) buys precision but blurs boundaries and can fabricate DMRs in sparse regions; MOABS CDIF and DSS shrinkage down-weight low-coverage sites, trading sensitivity for calibration.

BETA HETEROSCEDASTICITY AT 0/1: methylation beta is bounded; variance is largest near 0.5 and collapses near 0 and 1. Methods on raw beta (t-tests, BSmooth) are mis-calibrated at the extremes; arcsine (DSS-general) or M-value/logit (DMRcate via limma) transforms partially fix this but distort effect-size interpretation near the boundary -- exactly where many cancer hyper/hypo-methylation signals live.

REPLICATE REQUIREMENT vs SINGLE-SAMPLE POWER: rigorous biological-variance estimation needs replicates (BSmooth requires >=3 total samples; dmrseq permutation wants >=2/group; modkit MAP p-values need balanced replicates). With a SINGLE tumor vs SINGLE normal you cannot separate biological from sampling variance -- Fisher/methylKit-Fisher or modkit single-base run but report inflated confidence; the effect size (delta-beta, CDIF, Cohen's h) is the honest deliverable, not the p-value.

GERMLINE-vs-SOMATIC / ALLELIC CONFOUND: tumor-vs-normal DMRs conflate true somatic remethylation with pre-existing allele-specific methylation (ASM/imprinting) and germline mQTL. No off-the-shelf DMR tool controls for this -- it requires a haplotype-resolved design (precisely ISM's somatic-controlled HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis and normal-anchored cis-test).

COPY-NUMBER / PURITY / PLOIDY (cancer-specific): in a tumor, observed beta at a CpG is a mixture across copies, subclones and contaminating normal. A CNV gain or LOH shifts apparent beta with no change in true per-allele methylation -- a pure artifact DMR. None of these 9 tools model copy number or tumor purity; all assume a clean two-group comparison, so cancer somatic DMRs are confounded unless CN/purity-corrected upstream.

HETEROGENEITY / EPIPOLYMORPHISM: site-level tools collapse the read x CpG matrix to a single beta per group, discarding within-sample read-level heterogeneity (epialleles). A locus can have identical mean beta yet completely different epiallele structure between tumor and normal -- invisible to every DMR caller here. This is the structural blind spot that read-level methods (ISM's primary engine) exist to fill.

PHASING DEPENDENCE (for the somatic-controlled framing): site-level DM on a somatic haplotype axis (HP1 vs HP1-1) presupposes correct LOH-constrained phasing and accurate HP tagging; mis-phasing reassigns reads between axes and creates spurious delta-beta. Standard DMR tools have no phasing concept, so this confound is entirely upstream and silent.
axes.ism_difference: ISM's site-level axis (per-CpG Fisher exact + BH-FDR; Cramer's V with a Cochran minimum-expected-count gate; delta-beta = HP1-vs-HP1-1 mean-methylation difference with Wilcoxon + Cohen's d) is methodologically a SUBSET of the canonical DMP toolkit above -- essentially methylKit-Fisher plus an effect-size layer (delta-beta/Cohen's d, analogous to MOABS's CDIF and modkit's Cohen's h). Where ISM diverges from the entire AXIS-3 field is NOT the per-CpG statistic (which is conventional and, per the project's own findings, deliberately conservative) but (a) the COMPARISON AXIS and (b) where this axis sits in the method. Every tool above runs tumor-group-vs-normal-group and is therefore confounded by allele-specific methylation, germline mQTL, copy-number and purity; ISM instead runs a SOMATIC-CONTROLLED, haplotype-resolved HP1-vs-HP1-1 contrast (somatic allele vs its germline-matched counterpart on the same haplotype background) plus a NORMAL-ANCHORED cis-test (d_cis vs d_drift using the normal HP1 baseline) that explicitly separates true somatic cis-methylation from germline drift and copy -- a confound control none of the 9 standard DMR tools provides. The second, larger difference: in ISM the site-level axis is a CHARACTERIZATION / confirmation layer, deliberately NOT the primary engine. ISM's primary engine is the read-level NHD distance-matrix -> UPGMA/silhouette -> PERMANOVA structure test, which captures epipolymorphism and subclonal epiallele structure that all 9 site-level tools structurally discard (they collapse the read x CpG matrix to one beta per group). Conventional DMR callers also far exceed ISM in spatial-correlation machinery (dmrseq AR(1), comb-p autocorrelation, metilene CBS, DMRcate kernel, BSmooth/DSS smoothing) and in genome-wide region-level FDR -- ISM's site axis does per-CpG BH-FDR but no principled spatial region aggregation, because region structure is handled by the read-distance engine, not by smoothing CpG p-values. Finally, ISM's own AXIS-discrimination result (methylation tested as a TP/FP somatic-variant filter = NEGATIVE four ways; ASM real but not discriminative) is a finding these tools never make because they are built to call DMRs, not to ask whether a DMR can classify a variant -- ISM's contribution on this axis is the honest negative plus the haplotype-controlled, copy-aware framing, not a new per-site statistic.
axes.where_ism_sits: ISM's site-level axis is a SECONDARY characterization/confirmation layer (per-CpG Fisher + BH-FDR, Cramer's V + Cochran gate, delta-beta HP1-vs-HP1-1 Wilcoxon + Cohen's d), subordinate to ISM's PRIMARY read-distance engine (NHD matrix -> UPGMA/silhouette -> PERMANOVA). It overlaps the canonical DMP toolkit (approximately methylKit-Fisher + effect-size reporting like MOABS-CDIF / modkit-Cohen's h) on the statistic, but uniquely sits on a somatic-controlled haplotype axis with a normal-anchored cis-test for confound control, rather than the standard tumor-group-vs-normal-group contrast every external tool uses.

axes.axis: AXIS 4 — Methylation-based discrimination / ASM calling / classification (what the methylation signal is used to DISCRIMINATE: allele vs tissue vs tumor-fraction vs expression-driver vs true/false-variant)
axes.canonical_workflow: The field splits AXIS 4 into FOUR distinct discrimination targets, each with its own canonical pipeline: (1) ALLELE discrimination (ASM calling) — two sub-flavors: (a) SNP-anchored: call heterozygous SNVs -> partition reads by allele at each het SNP -> per-CpG/per-region compare methylation between the two allele bins via Fisher exact (sites) or t-test (regions) or moderated-t across conditions (DAMEfinder SNP mode, CGmapTools asr/ass); (b) phasing-FREE pattern-based: model each region's read-level methylation strings and fit a 1-allele (single binomial/Bernoulli) vs 2-allele (two-component mixture, each ~half the reads) model, then a likelihood-ratio test (methylpy/amrfinder, Fang 2012); DAMEfinder's tuple mode is a hybrid — co-methylation log-odds of adjacent CpG pairs (MM,UU vs MU,UM) weighted toward 50:50 balance. (2) TISSUE-OF-ORIGIN / DECONVOLUTION — define methylation haplotype blocks (MHB) by CpG-CpG co-methylation linkage, compute a block-level summary (MHL = weighted fraction of fully-methylated substrings), build a reference panel of tissue MHLs, then deconvolve a mixed (plasma cfDNA) sample as a non-negative mixture of references (Guo 2017 MHB/MHL; CancerLocator). (3) TUMOR-FRACTION — model plasma methylation as theta*tumor + (1-theta)*normal with Beta/Binomial likelihood, jointly MLE theta and tissue class (CancerLocator). (4) EXPRESSION-DRIVER — link per-gene methylation states to matched RNA expression via Beta-mixture states + inverse regression (MethylMix DM-value) or enhancer-probe-to-gene anti-correlation + TF-motif enrichment (ELMER). Canonical decision: pick the target FIRST (allele? tissue? fraction? driver?) because the test/statistic and the confounds differ entirely. ISM's AXIS 4 asked a FIFTH target nobody else in this survey directly tests: can ASM signal discriminate TRUE vs FALSE somatic variant calls (a variant-QC filter) — answer NEGATIVE.

tools.name: DAMEfinder
tools.what_it_does: R/Bioconductor ASM caller for bisulfite-seq. Two modes converging on differential ASM: (1) tuple mode = per adjacent-CpG-pair co-methylation log-odds; (2) SNP mode = reference-vs-alternative allele methylation difference. DISCRIMINATES: allele (allele-specific methylation) + condition-differential ASM.
tools.statistic: Tuple ASM score = log10[ (XMM+c)(XUU+c) / (XMU+c)(XUM+c) ] * w_i, where XMM/XUU/XMU/XUM are read-pair counts (meth-meth / unmeth-unmeth / mixed) over a CpG-pair tuple, c=pseudocount, weight w_i = P(0.5-eps < theta_i < 0.5+eps | XMM,XUU,gamma) with theta_i ~ Beta(gamma+XMM, gamma+XUU) -> upweights balanced ~50:50 bimodal (true ASM), penalizes random methylation. SNP ASM score = (XMir/Xir)-(XMia/Xia) = methylated-fraction on reference minus on alt allele. Differential ASM across conditions: limma lmFit + eBayes moderated t-statistic per CpG position.
tools.citation: Orjuela et al. 2020, Epigenetics & Chromatin 13:25. PMID 32487212; DOI 10.1186/s13072-020-00346-8. Verified via PMC7268773 full text + Bioconductor.
tools.cancer_or_germline: both (imprinting/XCI + cancer; explicitly cautions cancer intra-tumor heterogeneity)
tools.granularity: CpG-pair tuple and per-SNP region; cohort-level differential

tools.name: CGmapTools (asr / ass modes)
tools.what_it_does: Bisulfite-seq toolkit: improves heterozygous SNV calling (BayesWC) and detects ASM at site (ass) and region (asr) level by partitioning reads by SNP allele. DISCRIMINATES: allele (SNP-anchored).
tools.statistic: ass (sites): Fisher exact test on methylated/unmethylated counts of the two SNP-defined allele bins per CpG. asr (regions): Student's t-test across the CpG sites comparing the two alleles; corrected p<=0.05. ASM region criteria: >=2 CpG covered, hypo-allele mCG <=0.2 AND hyper-allele mCG >=0.8, corrected p<=0.05. Requires het SNVs first (BayesWC).
tools.citation: Guo et al. 2018, Bioinformatics 34(3):381-387. PMID 28968643; DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx595. Verified via Oxford Academic + official cgmaptools docs.
tools.cancer_or_germline: germline/general (SNP-anchored)

tools.name: methylpy / amrfinder (allelicmeth; Fang 2012 model)
tools.what_it_does: Phasing-FREE / SNP-free read-level ASM caller (MethPipe/methylpy). Input = Epiread-format mapped reads. DISCRIMINATES: allele WITHOUT genotype, purely from bimodal read-level methylation (~half reads one pattern, half the other).
tools.statistic: Per region fits two models: M0 = single methylation level for all reads (one allele/no ASM); M1 = two-component model, reads split into two methylation patterns each ~50% (two alleles). Log-likelihood-RATIO test M1 vs M0 scores ASM; per-region p/score flags allelically methylated regions (AMRs). Probabilistic model from Fang 2012.
tools.citation: Fang et al. 2012, PNAS 109(19):7332-7337. PMID 22523239; DOI 10.1073/pnas.1201310109. amrfinder: smithlabresearch.org/software/amrfinder. Abstract + tool page verified; full LRT in MethPipe manual, not re-derived.
tools.cancer_or_germline: germline (imprinting/ICR boundaries) primarily

tools.name: MHB / MHL (methylation haplotype block / load; Guo 2017)
tools.what_it_does: Defines methylation haplotype blocks (co-methylated CpG runs) + block summary statistic MHL; deconvolves heterogeneous tissue mixtures and maps tumor tissue-of-origin from plasma cfDNA. DISCRIMINATES: tissue-of-origin + tumor fraction (NOT allele).
tools.statistic: MHB defined by CpG-CpG co-methylation linkage disequilibrium (r^2 of adjacent CpG methylation states above cutoff) -> 147,888 blocks from 61 WGBS. MHL = normalized weighted mean of the fraction of fully-methylated substrings of length i within a block, weight w_i increasing with i (longer fully-methylated stretches upweighted); separates blocks with equal mean methylation but different co-methylation. Deconvolution = non-negative mixture of reference-tissue MHL profiles -> tumor load + tissue-of-origin in cfDNA.
tools.citation: Guo et al. 2017, Nature Genetics 49(4):635-642. PMID 28263317; DOI 10.1038/ng.3805. MHL formula cross-verified via secondary literature (JCEM dgaa950, Metheor); Nature full text paywalled.
tools.cancer_or_germline: cancer (cfDNA tumor TOO + load)

tools.name: CancerLocator
tools.what_it_does: Probabilistic deconvolution of plasma cfDNA methylation to simultaneously estimate tumor burden (fraction) and tissue-of-origin. DISCRIMINATES: tumor-fraction + tissue/cancer-type.
tools.statistic: Models plasma methylation x_k at CpG cluster k as mixture x_k = (1-theta)*v_k + theta*u_k (normal + tumor). Each tissue type ~ Beta(alpha_kt, beta_kt); reads m_k ~ Binomial(n_k, x_k). Maximum-likelihood jointly estimates theta (burden) and class t (tissue). Score lambda = (1/K)[ log L(theta_hat,t_hat|M,N) - log L(theta=0|M,N) ] normalized by feature count K. Reference learned from TCGA.
tools.citation: Kang et al. 2017, Genome Biology 18:53. PMID 28335812; DOI 10.1186/s13059-017-1191-5. Verified via PMC5364586 full text.
tools.platform: Methylation array / sequencing of cfDNA; reference = TCGA
tools.cancer_or_germline: cancer (cfDNA diagnosis + TOO)
tools.granularity: genome-wide CpG-cluster feature set; sample-level output

tools.name: MethylMix (DM-value)
tools.what_it_does: Identifies methylation-DRIVEN cancer genes by linking per-gene methylation states to matched expression. DISCRIMINATES: expression-driver (functional methylation), NOT allele or tissue.
tools.statistic: Per-CpG/gene Beta-mixture model (component count by BIC) defines discrete methylation STATES; DM-value = state mean minus normal-tissue mean (Wilcoxon rank-sum vs normal). Transcriptionally-predictive filter: keep only genes with significant INVERSE methylation-expression association (linear regression, p<0.01).
tools.citation: Gevaert 2015, Bioinformatics 31(11):1839-1841. PMID 25609794; DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btv020. Verified via PMC4443673.
tools.cancer_or_germline: cancer (driver-gene discovery)

tools.name: ELMER v.2
tools.what_it_does: Reconstructs gene regulatory networks from paired methylation + transcriptome: links distal enhancer probe methylation to target-gene expression and upstream master-regulator TFs. DISCRIMINATES: expression-driver / cis-regulatory (enhancer->gene->TF), NOT allele.
tools.statistic: Per distal (enhancer) probe-gene pair: test inverse correlation between probe methylation and gene expression (Mann-Whitney U on unmethylated-vs-methylated groups); enrich TF-binding motifs within significant probes; rank master-regulator TFs by anti-correlation of TF expression with methylation of distal probes within 250 bp of the motif.
tools.citation: Silva et al. 2019, Bioinformatics 35(11):1974-1977 'ELMER v.2'. PMID 30364927; DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty902.
tools.cancer_or_germline: cancer (regulatory network)

difficulties: GERMLINE-vs-SOMATIC CONFOUND (central AXIS-4 pain point): SNP-anchored callers (CGmapTools asr/ass, DAMEfinder SNP mode) partition reads by a het SNP and CANNOT tell whether the allelic methylation difference is germline/imprinting baseline ASM or somatic-specific — they measure REF-vs-ALT, which in ISM's internal work is the confounded ALLELE-axis (TP 11.1% < het-null 15.2%). Only a somatic-controlled axis (HP1 germline vs HP1-1 somatic-on-same-haplotype via LOH-constrained phasing) isolates somatic ASM. None of the surveyed tools build this somatic-controlled axis.

TUMOR HETEROGENEITY / EPIPOLYMORPHISM vs true ASM: DAMEfinder explicitly states it is 'very difficult to discern heterogeneity from real ASM' in bisulfite-seq alone and does not model intra-tumor heterogeneity. A subclonal mixture produces a bimodal read-level pattern that the 1-vs-2-allele LRT (amrfinder/Fang) and the tuple 50:50 weight (DAMEfinder) score AS IF allelic, so a high ASM score can be subclonal drift, not cis-allelic regulation — the same failure mode ISM guards against with the normal-anchored cis-test (d_cis vs d_drift).

COPY-NUMBER / LOH confound: allelic methylation ratios are distorted when the two alleles are at unequal copy number (cnLOH gives one allele 2 copies, 0 of the other). SNP-allele read counts no longer reflect 1:1 chromosomes, biasing the hypo<=0.2/hyper>=0.8 thresholds (CGmapTools) and the REF-ALT delta (DAMEfinder SNP). No surveyed allele caller corrects for somatic CN; cfDNA tools (CancerLocator/MHL) assume reference-tissue profiles unperturbed by CN.

SINGLE-SAMPLE POWER / COHORT REQUIREMENT: MethylMix needs ~>=100 samples for Beta-mixture states; DAMEfinder differential ASM and ELMER need cohorts; CancerLocator/MHL need a curated reference PANEL (TCGA tissues). A single ONT cancer genome can only make per-sample ASM-existence calls, capping statistical tier (ISM's own single-sample HCC1395 ceiling).

COVERAGE & PHASING DEPENDENCE: ASM scoring needs enough reads PER ALLELE/haplotype; DAMEfinder cites ~10x minimum for SNP calling and ASM scores are noisy at low per-allele depth. SNP-anchored methods fail in SNP-deserts and at LOH sites (no het SNP to partition). Phasing-free methods (amrfinder) avoid genotype but still need a clean bimodal read split, degraded by epipolymorphism.

BISULFITE/SHORT-READ ORIGIN — TOOL-CONTEXT MISMATCH: every surveyed tool was built for SHORT-READ BISULFITE (5mC only, no 5hmC distinction, short fragments => few co-CpG per read, limited SNP-CpG co-phasing). ONT long reads natively carry 5mC+5hmC (MM/ML) AND span many CpG + het SNPs on one molecule, so read-level haplotype methylation is observed directly — the long-read regime is OUTSIDE these tools' design envelope; re-implementing tuple/MHL co-methylation on long reads is non-trivial and is where ISM operates.

THE OPEN QUESTION — can ASM discriminate TRUE vs FALSE variant calls? NONE of the surveyed tools target variant-QC; all assume the variant/SNP is real and ask about methylation around it. ISM directly tested ASM as a TP/FP somatic-variant filter and found NEGATIVE four independent ways (ASM real but anti-discriminative — strong-ASM 5x enriched in FP, OR=0.194, p=1.8e-28). The discrimination-as-filter framing is an ISM-specific contribution with a definitive negative answer, not a gap others solved.

TUMOR PURITY: low ctDNA fraction collapses CancerLocator's tissue-of-origin signal (theta MLE unstable at low burden, stated limitation) and dilutes tumor-specific ASM below germline/normal background in bulk tissue — purity is a hard floor on every AXIS-4 discrimination target.
axes.ism_difference: ISM's AXIS-4 (discrimination) differs in TARGET and in CONFOUND CONTROL. (1) TARGET: surveyed tools each discriminate ONE of {allele (DAMEfinder/CGmapTools/amrfinder), tissue-of-origin (MHB/MHL/CancerLocator), tumor-fraction (CancerLocator), expression-driver (MethylMix/ELMER)}. ISM instead asked whether methylation can discriminate TRUE-vs-FALSE somatic variant calls (a variant-QC filter) — a target none address — and answered NEGATIVE four independent ways (ASM real but not discriminative; strong-ASM 5x enriched in FP, OR=0.194, p=1.8e-28), reframing AXIS-4 from filter to CHARACTERIZATION. (2) SOMATIC-CONTROLLED AXIS: every SNP-anchored surveyed caller compares REF-vs-ALT (the germline/imprinting-confounded ALLELE axis). ISM uniquely builds HP1(germline) vs HP1-1(somatic-on-same-haplotype) from LOH-constrained phasing, holding copy-number/ploidy/alignment constant — directly addressing the germline-vs-somatic confound DAMEfinder names as unsolved. (3) NORMAL-ANCHORED cis-TEST: ISM adds a normal HP1 baseline and contrasts d_cis vs d_drift to separate true somatic cis-ASM from cohesion/heterogeneity drift — operationalizing the 'heterogeneity vs real ASM' problem DAMEfinder flags as 'very difficult'. (4) ENGINE: ISM's PRIMARY engine is not a per-CpG allele test but a read-to-read NHD distance matrix -> UPGMA + silhouette -> PERMANOVA(pseudo-F) structure test on subclonal groups, with the per-CpG Fisher / Delta-beta / Cramer-V layer as SECONDARY site-level confirmation. The surveyed tools have no read-level multivariate structure test; their closest analogues are amrfinder's 2-component read-pattern LRT and DAMEfinder's CpG-pair tuple — both far simpler than a permutation-based multivariate clustering test on long-read 5mC+5hmC matrices.
axes.where_ism_sits: ISM sits at the intersection of AXIS-4 ALLELE-discrimination and a NEW variant-QC discrimination target, executed on ONT LONG-READ 5mC+5hmC matrices with a somatic-controlled (HP1-vs-HP1-1) axis and a read-level multivariate structure engine — a regime no surveyed tool occupies. Surveyed allele callers (DAMEfinder/CGmapTools/amrfinder) are short-read bisulfite, SNP/pattern-anchored, germline-confounded, per-CpG; the deconvolution/driver tools (MHL/CancerLocator/MethylMix/ELMER) target tissue/fraction/expression, not allele or variant-QC. ISM's empirically-grounded conclusion (ASM exists and is somatic-real but is NOT a usable TP/FP filter -> characterization, not filter) is its distinctive AXIS-4 position, and the normal-anchored cis-test is the unique control separating somatic cis-ASM from germline drift + copy-number — the exact confounds every surveyed tool leaves open.

pain_points.name: Coverage requirements (which metrics need >10x; ASM needs ~2x bulk)
pain_points.description: Per-CpG and per-read methylation metrics have hard coverage floors. Bulk single-CpG 5mC fraction is usable at ~5-10x (e.g., 5mC-CpG reaches F1>0.9 at ~5x by direct ONT calling), but READ-LEVEL heterogeneity metrics (PDR, FDRP/qFDRP, epipolymorphism) need substantially more because they require multiple INFORMATIVE reads each spanning >=4 CpGs at the same locus: Scherer 2020 recommends minimum coverage of 10 at individual CpGs for FDRP/qFDRP and caps sampling at 40 reads/CpG to avoid combinatorial explosion, and Landau's PDR is only computed over reads covering >=4 CpGs. ALLELE-SPECIFIC methylation (ASM) is worst: phasing splits reads across two haplotypes so each haplotype gets ~half the depth, so reliable ASM effectively needs ~2x the bulk coverage (NANOME recommends >=15x per-haplotype, implying ~30x total). Other ONT marks (6mA) need >=20x for F1=0.9. ALGORITHM/STAT: F1-vs-coverage benchmarking curves; per-CpG binomial sampling noise scales as 1/sqrt(n_reads), so beta(meth) CI width and minimum detectable methylation difference shrink only with depth.
pain_points.source: Scherer et al. 2020, Nucleic Acids Res 48(8):e46, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaa120, PMID 32103242 (min coverage 10 for FDRP/qFDRP; 40-read cap) [VERIFIED]. Landau et al. 2014, Cancer Cell 26(6):813-825, DOI 10.1016/j.ccell.2014.10.012, PMID 25490447 (PDR needs reads spanning >=4 CpGs) [VERIFIED]. NANOME, Liu et al. 2025 bioRxiv, DOI 10.1101/2025.06.29.662079, PMID 40631091 (>=15x maintains performance; ASM splits depth across haplotypes) [VERIFIED].
pain_points.how_field_handles: Coverage-vs-F1 benchmarking to set per-metric floors; cap reads/CpG to bound combinatorics (Scherer 40-read cap); require >=4 CpGs/read for read-level scores; target ~30x total ONT for ASM so each haplotype gets ~15x (NANOME); use consensus callers (NANOME XGBoost over Megalodon/Nanopolish/DeepSignal, +4% F1 at discordant regions) to lower the per-read error floor and effectively reduce the coverage needed.

pain_points.name: Tumor heterogeneity / epipolymorphism / PDR (intratumor stochastic methylation)
pain_points.description: A bulk tumor is a polyclonal mixture, so a single locus shows MIXED epialleles within and across reads; this is not noise but a measurable, clinically relevant signal that breaks the assumption of one methylation state per allele. Three canonical read-level statistics quantify it. (1) PDR (Landau 2014): a read is CONCORDANT if all its CpGs share one state, DISCORDANT if mixed; PDR = discordant/total reads over reads covering >=4 CpGs. Higher PDR = locally disordered/stochastic methylation, associated with shorter remission in CLL. (2) Epipolymorphism (Landan 2012): over a 4-CpG window (2^4=16 possible epialleles), EPM = probability that two randomly sampled epialleles differ = 1 - sum(p_i^2). (3) FDRP/qFDRP (Scherer 2020): fraction of read PAIRS discordant at overlapping CpGs; qFDRP weights by Hamming distance to resist single-CpG flips. These metrics confound trivially with read depth and CpG density, and with normal-cell admixture (a mixture LOOKS heterogeneous even with two internally-homogeneous clones).
pain_points.source: Landau et al. 2014, Cancer Cell 26(6):813-825, DOI 10.1016/j.ccell.2014.10.012, PMID 25490447 (PDR; RRBS+WGBS; PDR -> shorter remission) [VERIFIED]. Landan et al. 2012, Nat Genet 44:1207, DOI 10.1038/ng.2442 (epipolymorphism, 16 epialleles, stochastic DMR formation over 300 generations) [search-summarized, abstract-level; UNVERIFIED at full text]. Scherer et al. 2020, NAR 48(8):e46, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaa120, PMID 32103242 (FDRP/qFDRP; qFDRP most robust to noise, best tumor-purity predictor r=0.966) [VERIFIED].
pain_points.which_axes: tumor heterogeneity/epipolymorphism/PDR; coverage; tumor purity (admixture mimics heterogeneity); read/CpG-density confound
pain_points.how_field_handles: Use read-level (not pooled-fraction) statistics that exploit ONT long reads phasing many CpGs per molecule; prefer qFDRP for robustness to technical noise and CpG density (Scherer benchmark); require >=4 CpGs/read; report heterogeneity AND mean methylation jointly since they decouple; ONT epialleles avoid the short-read fragmentation that truncates epiallele length in WGBS/RRBS.

pain_points.name: Germline-vs-somatic ASM confound (imprinting + cis-haplotype ASM masquerade as cancer ASM)
pain_points.description: Allele-specific methylation in a tumor has at least three origins that are hard to separate: (a) genomic IMPRINTING (parent-of-origin, ~150 gene domains, 50/50 allele-switching between individuals); (b) germline cis-acting genotype/haplotype-dependent ASM (hap-ASM) driven by SNPs disrupting CTCF/TF binding motifs; and (c) genuine cancer/somatic de novo ASM. A naive ASM scan flags all three. The danger for somatic methylation work: a het-SNP/haplotype baseline ASM (germline) will be present in BOTH alleles of a tumor read set and is NOT somatic — so an ALT-vs-REF allelic methylation difference cannot distinguish somatic-specific ASM from this germline baseline without a matched control. ALGORITHM/STAT: Do 2020 used allele-switching frequency (only ~3% of recurrent non-imprinted ASM showed >=20% inter-individual switching vs ~90% for known imprinted genes), GeneImprint annotation to drop imprinted regions, and SNP/CTCF-TF motif disruption analysis; cancer-specific de novo ASM was isolated by paired tumor-normal comparison and filtering variants within 1 kb of known ASM index SNPs.
pain_points.source: Do et al. 2020, Genome Biology 21:153, DOI 10.1186/s13059-020-02059-3, PMID 32594908 (15,112 non-imprinted recurrent ASM DMRs; ASM 5-9x higher in cancer vs lineage-matched normal; 6-17% of somatic mutations -> de novo ASM gains; 71% of de novo ASM TF motifs match germline-ASM motif classes -> shared mechanism) [VERIFIED]. Akbari et al. 2022 (imprinted DMR detection via NanoMethPhase), eLife 11:e77898, DOI 10.7554/eLife.77898, PMID 35787786 (germline gDMR vs somatic sDMR classification via oocyte/sperm/blastocyst methylation) [VERIFIED].
pain_points.which_axes: germline-vs-somatic ASM confound; phasing-dependence; tumor purity (need matched normal)
pain_points.how_field_handles: Mandatory MATCHED-NORMAL comparison to subtract germline/imprinting baseline; flag and drop annotated imprinted regions (GeneImprint); allele-switching-frequency test to separate imprinting (high inter-individual switch) from somatic; require the somatic axis to be the haplotype-internal (HP1 vs HP1-subclone) contrast rather than ALT-vs-REF which is germline-confounded; cis-motif (CTCF/TF) disruption analysis to attribute genotype-driven ASM; for imprinting specifically, parent-of-origin phasing via trios + reference-tissue methylation (oocyte/sperm) to classify germline vs somatic DMRs.

pain_points.name: Copy-number driving apparent allelic methylation (CNA confound)
pain_points.description: Copy-number alterations change the RATIO of methylated to unmethylated alleles purely arithmetically, producing apparent ASM/methylation change with NO epigenetic alteration. In a normal diploid imprinted locus the 1:1 allele ratio gives ~50% methylation; an amplification to 4:1 yields 75:25 or 25:75 depending on which parental allele is amplified. So allelic imbalance (amplification, deletion, cnLOH) shifts the observed methylation fraction mechanically. This is the single largest driver of apparent imprinting/ASM aberration in tumors. ALGORITHM/STAT: Martin-Trujillo 2017 computed a CNA-PREDICTED methylation value from copy number and minor-allele counts, used univariate linear regression to estimate the fraction of methylation variance explained by copy number (R^2), and only called a TRUE epigenetic change when observed methylation fell outside +/-3 s.d. of the CNA-predicted value from normal-tissue controls. Result: in copy-number-NORMAL samples only 8-17.6% of imprinted regions showed CNA-independent methylation change -> CNAs explain MOST apparent imprinting aberration. CAMDAC formalizes the deconvolution: observed bulk tumor methylation rate is modeled as a function of tumor purity, allele-specific copy number, and the normal-cell methylation fraction, then inverted to recover the pure-tumor allele-specific methylation rate.
pain_points.source: Martin-Trujillo et al. 2017, Nat Commun 8:467, DOI 10.1038/s41467-017-00639-9, PMID 28883545 (CN ratio mechanism; regression R^2; +/-3 s.d. rule; 8.1-17.6% CNA-independent) [VERIFIED]. CAMDAC, Pancaldi/Van Loo lab, bioRxiv DOI 10.1101/2020.11.03.366252 (copy-number-aware methylation deconvolution from tumor-normal RRBS -> purity, allele-specific CN, polymorphism-independent tumor methylation rate; applied to 122 TRACERx NSCLC samples) [VERIFIED via search+biorxiv summary].
pain_points.which_axes: copy-number confound; tumor purity (CAMDAC models both jointly); germline-vs-somatic ASM (cnLOH creates allelic imbalance)
pain_points.how_field_handles: Compute CNA-predicted methylation and subtract/regress it out (Martin-Trujillo +/-3 s.d. gate); copy-number-aware deconvolution that JOINTLY models purity + allele-specific CN to recover pure-tumor methylation (CAMDAC); design contrasts that hold CN constant (e.g., HP-axis within a single haplotype/genomic position rather than ALLELE-axis across amplified/deleted alleles); test methylation change for correlation with local allelic copy number and reject CN-driven signals; use partial correlation against continuous CN ground-truth to confirm a signal is not CN-driven.

pain_points.name: Single-sample statistical power (no replicates)
pain_points.description: Cancer somatic ONT studies very often have ONE tumor (and maybe one matched normal), no biological replicates. Without replicates you cannot estimate BIOLOGICAL (between-sample) variance, only sampling/technical variance — yet methylation dispersion varies substantially genome-wide, so a single dispersion assumption is wrong. The naive fix (pool counts + Fisher's exact test on methylated/unmethylated read counts per CpG) IGNORES biological variance and inflates false positives, because it conflates sampling noise with true between-cell variation. ALGORITHM/STAT: DSS-single (Wu 2015) models BS read counts with a beta-binomial (binomial = sampling, beta with dispersion phi = biological variance), borrows information across the genome with a log-normal prior, and crucially uses SPATIAL CORRELATION — nearby CpGs as 'pseudo-replicates' via local smoothing — to estimate per-site dispersion even with n=1, enabling a valid Wald-type test. It outperforms Fisher's exact and raw-methylation-difference at the CpG level. The deeper problem in cancer: a single sample cannot separate a real somatic effect from sample-specific idiosyncrasy / circularity, so single-sample positives are tier-capped and need cross-sample/held-out replication.
pain_points.source: Wu et al. 2015 (DSS-single), Nucleic Acids Res 43(21):e141, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkv715, PMID 26184873 (beta-binomial; nearby-CpG pseudo-replicates for dispersion; Fisher pooling -> false positives) [VERIFIED].
pain_points.which_axes: single-sample power; tumor heterogeneity (dispersion varies genome-wide); coverage
pain_points.how_field_handles: Beta-binomial dispersion modeling with nearby-CpG pseudo-replicates instead of pooled Fisher (DSS-single); permutation / HP-shuffle nulls to set a sample-specific significance floor; matched-normal as the within-sample control; LOSO / held-out and cross-sample replication to break single-sample circularity and cap claims (single-pipeline single-sample findings tier-capped pending independent samples).

pain_points.name: Tumor purity (normal-cell admixture dilutes and distorts methylation)
pain_points.description: Bulk tumor DNA is a mixture of cancer + stromal/immune/normal cells. The observed methylation fraction at every CpG is a purity-weighted average: beta_obs = p*beta_tumor + (1-p)*beta_normal (further weighted by per-allele copy number under CNA). Low purity drags tumor-specific hyper/hypomethylation toward the normal value, shrinking effect sizes and killing power; it also makes a pure-but-heterogeneous tumor INDISTINGUISHABLE from an admixed homogeneous one in read-level heterogeneity scores (admixture inflates PDR/epipolymorphism). Purity and copy number are entangled and must be solved together. ALGORITHM/STAT: CAMDAC infers purity, ploidy and allele-specific copy number from the bulk methylome + matched normal, then algebraically inverts the mixture+CN model to deconvolve the pure-tumor (allele-specific) methylation rate per CpG, enabling unbiased tumor-normal and tumor-tumor differential methylation; qFDRP was shown to predict tumor purity (cross-validated r=0.966), i.e. purity directly drives heterogeneity scores.
pain_points.source: CAMDAC, bioRxiv DOI 10.1101/2020.11.03.366252 (purity + allele-specific CN deconvolution from tumor-normal RRBS; 122 TRACERx NSCLC) [VERIFIED via search+biorxiv summary]. Scherer et al. 2020, NAR 48(8):e46, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaa120, PMID 32103242 (qFDRP predicts purity r=0.966 -> purity confounds heterogeneity scores) [VERIFIED]. Martin-Trujillo et al. 2017, DOI 10.1038/s41467-017-00639-9, PMID 28883545 (purity considered alongside CN as bulk-methylation confound) [VERIFIED].
pain_points.which_axes: tumor purity; copy-number (jointly modeled); tumor heterogeneity (admixture mimics it); single-sample power (effect-size shrinkage)
pain_points.how_field_handles: Estimate purity (from VAF/CN or from the methylome itself) and deconvolve via the purity+CN mixture model (CAMDAC: beta_obs = f(purity, allele-specific CN, beta_normal)); always use matched normal to anchor beta_normal; report effect sizes purity-corrected; recognize purity drives read-level heterogeneity scores so adjust/stratify; for ONT, haplotype-resolved tumor reads partially sidestep bulk admixture by isolating tumor-haplotype reads.

pain_points.name: Phasing dependence + LOH losing het anchors
pain_points.description: ASM and haplotype-resolved methylation REQUIRE phasing reads to haplotypes, which depends on heterozygous SNVs along/spanning the reads. Two failure modes: (1) SNV deserts — if a read does not span two het SNVs, its haplotype is unknown and a phase block breaks (only ~95% of autosomal CpGs were phaseable even in a clean trio setting; the unphased ~5% concentrate in low-complexity/blacklist regions). (2) LOH — loss of heterozygosity (common in cancer, including cnLOH) REMOVES heterozygous sites, so exactly the cancer-relevant regions (deletions, copy-neutral LOH) lose their het anchors and become unphaseable by SNVs, precisely where allelic methylation might matter most.
