ALGORITHM/STAT: MethPhaser bridges SNV-sparse/LOH gaps by treating haplotype-differential methylation as a phasing signal — Wilcoxon rank-sum test (p<0.05) on per-CpG modification scores between SNV-haplotagged reads to find haplotype-specific CpGs, then iteratively assigns unphased reads by their methylation pattern (>=3 votes default) and connects neighboring phase blocks. It raised HG002 phase N50 from 1.7 Mb to 4.0 Mb (1.6-2.55x across populations) with only ~1.3% switch error per connection and +0.02% flip rate. NanoMethPhase/NANOME use single-sample het SNVs (no trio) for haplotagging, contingent on enough het variants.
pain_points.source: MethPhaser, Fu et al. 2024, Nat Commun 15:5327, DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-49588-0, PMID 38909018 (SNV-desert/homozygosity phase breaks; methylation-Wilcoxon bridging; N50 1.7->4.0 Mb) [VERIFIED]. Akbari et al. 2022, eLife 11:e77898, DOI 10.7554/eLife.77898, PMID 35787786 (~95% CpGs phaseable; unphased 5% map to ENCODE blacklist) [VERIFIED]. Gershman/NanoMethPhase, Genome Biol 2021 22:68, DOI 10.1186/s13059-021-02283-5 (megabase methylation phasing from het SNVs at ~10x) [search-verified].
pain_points.which_axes: phasing-dependence + LOH; coverage (per-haplotype depth); germline-vs-somatic (phasing needed to define the somatic HP-axis)
pain_points.how_field_handles: Use long ONT reads to span more het SNVs per fragment (longer phase blocks than short reads); methylation-based phase-block bridging across SNV deserts / LOH (MethPhaser Wilcoxon + voting); single-sample het-SNV haplotagging without trios (NanoMethPhase/NANOME/Clair3); accept that LOH regions may be intrinsically unphaseable by SNVs and either fall back to methylation-only phasing or exclude them; report fraction of CpGs/genome phaseable as a coverage-of-conclusion caveat.

pain_points.name: 5mC/5hmC distinction (mark conflation)
pain_points.description: Standard bisulfite/RRBS/WGBS CANNOT distinguish 5mC from 5hmC: both resist bisulfite conversion and read as C (5hmC -> cytosine-5-methylenesulfonate, still pairs as C), so every 'methylation' call is actually 5mC+5hmC combined. This matters in cancer because 5hmC (the TET-oxidation intermediate) is globally DEPLETED in many tumors and has distinct, often opposite, regulatory meaning from 5mC; conflating them mis-assigns direction and magnitude of 'methylation' change. ONT can in principle resolve them directly (single-molecule current differs by mark), removing the need for oxBS/TAB-seq chemistry, but per-read separation of 5mC vs 5hmC is the hardest discrimination — accuracy is model/training-dependent (e.g., DeepMod ~0.99 precision for 5mC but 5hmC separation is weaker), and naive max-collapse over a 5mC+5hmC two-channel call can halve or distort the per-position fraction if not handled (an analysis artifact). ALGORITHM/STAT: oxidative bisulfite (oxBS, Booth 2012) oxidizes 5hmC->5fC->U so subtracting oxBS from BS gives 5hmC quantitatively; ONT basecallers emit separate 5mC/5hmC probabilities per CpG per read (MM/ML tags) requiring a model trained on both marks.
pain_points.source: 5hmC detection review, Bohrer/BMB Rep 2024, DOI 10.5483/BMBRep.2023-0250, PMID 38449301 (bisulfite conflates 5mC/5hmC via CMS; nanopore direct detection, accuracy model-dependent, DeepMod ~0.99 for 5mC) [VERIFIED]. Booth et al. 2012/2013 oxBS-seq, Nat Protoc/Science, PMID 24008380, DOI 10.1038/nprot.2013.115 (oxBS single-base 5mC vs 5hmC) [search-verified, abstract-level]. ONT single/double-stranded 5mC+5hmC, Commun Biol 2025, DOI 10.1038/s42003-025-07681-0 [search-found; full text UNVERIFIED behind redirect].
pain_points.which_axes: 5mC/5hmC distinction; coverage (two-channel call splits evidence per read); direction-of-effect in cancer
pain_points.how_field_handles: Use ONT basecallers trained to emit separate 5mC and 5hmC probabilities (MM/ML tags) rather than a single 'modified-C' call; or oxBS/TAB-seq chemistry to subtract one mark; be explicit which mark(s) a 'methylation' value represents and avoid silently max-collapsing a 5mC+5hmC two-channel call (an artifact that can halve the fraction); in cancer, treat global 5hmC loss as a distinct axis from 5mC gain; validate ONT mark-separation against oxBS on the same sample where possible.

pipeline.axis: Axis 1 — Phase → haplotag → per-haplotype methylation → DMR (the dominant "allele/haplotype-resolved methylation" production pipeline for cancer long-read ONT). This is the canonical, widely-cited workflow that InterSubMod's read-level ISM approach must position against.
pipeline.canonical_workflow:
CANONICAL 5-STAGE PIPELINE (region/locus-level, haplotype-resolved):

STAGE 1 — SNV CALLING (germline het variants are the phasing backbone):
  Tool: Clair3 (O'Neill POG used Clair3 v0.1-r8). Older NanoMethPhase docs/papers used Clair3 or comparable; the germline het SNVs are what anchor phasing. Output: VCF of het SNVs.

STAGE 2 — PHASING (assign het SNVs to two parental haplotypes):
  Tool: WhatsHap (bundled with Clair3; the de-facto standard for read-backed phasing). LongPhase is the faster alternative used in this lab's own stack. Output: phased VCF (GT with '|', e.g. 0|1 / 1|0, plus PS phase-set blocks).

STAGE 3 — HAPLOTAGGING (assign each READ to HP1/HP2 by overlapping phased het SNVs):
  Tool: WhatsHap haplotag OR NanoMethPhase phase module (O'Neill used NanoMethPhase v1.2.0 to phase reads+methylation). Output: BAM with HP:i:1 / HP:i:2 tags per read. Reads not spanning a het SNV remain untagged (HP absent).

STAGE 4 — PER-HAPLOTYPE METHYLATION PILEUP (collapse modBAM into per-HP CpG methylation fraction):
  Methylation calling upstream: 5mC called from raw signal — Nanopolish (O'Neill v0.13.3; NanoMethPhase native input) OR modern modbam (Dorado/Remora MM/ML tags). 
  Per-HP aggregation: 
    (a) modkit pileup with `--phased` (emits hp1.bedmethyl / hp2.bedmethyl / combined.bedmethyl, diploid only) OR the more general `--partition-tag HP` (emits <prefix>_1.bed / _2.bed by SAM tag value).
    (b) NanoMethPhase phase module emits per-haplotype methylation-frequency files directly.
  Output: two bedMethyl tables = methylation fraction per CpG per haplotype.

STAGE 5 — DMR / aDMR CALLING (test HP1 vs HP2 methylation difference per region):
  Two canonical statistical engines:
    (a) DSS R/Bioconductor (DMLtest -> callDML -> callDMR), which NanoMethPhase's `dma` module wraps. Beta-binomial / smoothed t-like Wald per-CpG, aggregated to regions. O'Neill POG used DSS v2.46 for aDMR significance. This is the dominant statistic in the cancer literature.
    (b) modkit dmr pair / dmr multi: log marginal likelihood-ratio test on Beta-Binomial (binary) / Dirichlet-Multinomial (multi-state) counts with Jeffreys prior; MAP-based p-value from posterior odds; Cohen's h effect size with 95% CI per region/segment.
  Output: aDMRs = allelically differentially methylated regions (regions where one haplotype is methylated and the other is not).

KEY FRAMING: The unit of inference is the REGION (DMR) summarising many CpGs across the two collapsed haplotype pileups. The biological hypothesis tested is allele-specific / haplotype-specific methylation (one parental allele methylated). This is a fundamentally 2-group (HP1 vs HP2), region-level, pileup-collapsed comparison.

difficulties: PHASING FAILURE IN LOW-SNP / REPETITIVE / LOH REGIONS: O'Neill explicitly documents that several modest-size tumor suppressors (BRCA1, NF1, RB1) could be phased completely in only ~half of tumors due to low SNP density + repetitive sequence. They state phasing 'can face challenges from the presence of structural and copy number variation (especially LOH)'. LOH erases het SNVs -> no phasing backbone -> region drops out of the haplotype-resolved analysis entirely. This is the single biggest blind spot of the canonical pipeline and exactly the cancer-specific regime ISM targets.

COVERAGE SPLIT PER HAPLOTYPE: Haplotagging halves usable depth — each haplotype only gets ~half the reads. O'Neill ran at median 17.5x (normal) / 26x (tumor) haploid coverage, well below the 80-120x typical of short-read WGBS, and flag this as a limitation. modkit --phased is diploid-only. Low per-HP depth weakens per-CpG beta-binomial estimates and DMR power; NanoMethPhase's headline claim is that ~10x total is the practical floor for ASM detection.

UNTAGGED READS DISCARDED: Only reads spanning at least one phased het SNV get an HP tag. Reads in long homozygous stretches (or LOH) carry no HP tag and are excluded from the per-HP pileup, so the aDMR analysis is restricted to ~84% (median 86%, SD 7.1%) of CpG sites that are phaseable — the rest are simply not interrogated allele-specifically.

GERMLINE IMPRINTING / CONSTITUTIVE ASM CONFOUND: A haplotype methylation difference can be a normal imprinted DMR or random monoallelic ASM rather than a tumor event. O'Neill had to explicitly EXCLUDE aDMRs 'associated with normal cell function (linked to imprinting or random allele-specific methylation)', dropping from 4.46M raw aDMRs to ~462K tumor-specific aDMRs. Without a matched normal or an imprinting blacklist, the pipeline cannot tell somatic ASM from constitutive ASM — a structural confounder of the whole axis.

REGION/PILEUP COLLAPSE LOSES READ-LEVEL HETEROGENEITY: DSS and modkit dmr both operate on COLLAPSED per-HP methylation fractions (counts of methylated/total at each CpG). The within-haplotype read-to-read pattern (epipolymorphism, subclonal mosaicism, cis-coordination along a single molecule) is averaged away. The unit of inference is the 2-group region comparison, not the individual molecule.

BINARY 2-HAPLOTYPE FRAME: The canonical workflow is hard-coded to exactly two haplotypes (diploid). It cannot natively represent >2 sub-haplotype groups or somatic copy-number-amplified haplotypes (HP1-1/HP2-1-style sub-splits), which is where subclonal structure lives.

HUGE RAW aDMR COUNT NEEDS HEAVY FILTERING: O'Neill found a mean 23.6K aDMRs/tumor (SD 14.6K; 4.46M total; ~5x more in tumor than matched normal mean 4.7K). The raw rate is dominated by noise/imprinting and only becomes interpretable after aggressive normal-subtraction and imprinting exclusion — recurrence is rare (RET intragenic-promoter aDMR in only 26 samples, CDKN2A in 9 samples), so per-locus somatic aDMR signal is sparse.
pipeline.ism_difference:
WHERE ISM DIVERGES FROM THIS BASELINE — the canonical axis-1 pipeline is REGION-level, PILEUP-COLLAPSED, 2-HAPLOTYPE, and SNV-phasing-dependent. ISM (InterSubMod) differs on every one of these:

(1) READ-LEVEL, NOT PILEUP-COLLAPSED. The DSS/modkit-dmr engines reduce each haplotype to a per-CpG methylated/total count and test a 2-group region difference; they discard the read x CpG matrix. ISM keeps the per-molecule methylation pattern and works in read-level distance space (read-read distance matrix + PERMANOVA / ARI clustering), so it can see within-haplotype heterogeneity (subclonal mosaicism, epipolymorphism) that the pileup averages out. Internal work confirms latent HP-substructure (487 'latent' loci: gated CramersV=0 but PERMANOVA-significant) invisible to count-collapsed DMR tests.

(2) DOES NOT REQUIRE SNV PHASING TO EXIST — directly addresses the LOH blind spot. The whole canonical axis collapses where het SNVs vanish (LOH, low-SNP, repetitive), which is precisely the cancer regime. ISM's read-level methylation clustering can probe structure where there is no phasing backbone (and internal results show methylation operates at germline-haplotype resolution: strong at separating different haplotypes, weak within-haplotype subgroups — T1/T2 positive, T3 negative).

(3) DIFFERENT QUESTION (two answers, not one). The DMR axis answers 'is HP1 != HP2 methylation here?' (existence/discrimination conflated into one region p-value). ISM separates 'does allele/haplotype methylation structure EXIST' (broadly YES, ~3-4% of loci, cross-cancer reproducible) from 'is it USABLE as a TP/FP variant filter' (NO — low sensitivity ~4%, COLO829 TP≈FP, anti-discriminative at strong-ASM loci). The canonical pipeline never makes this existence-vs-usability split.

(4) SOMATIC-CONTROLLED AXIS. modkit/DSS test HP1-vs-HP2 (ALLELE axis), which is confounded by baseline germline-het ASM and imprinting — the same confounder O'Neill had to blacklist. ISM additionally uses an HP-axis / sub-haplotype-matched design (HP1 vs HP1-1) that holds CN/ploidy/alignment constant, giving a somatic-controlled contrast the canonical 2-group DMR cannot.

POSITIONING: ISM is NOT a competitor DMR caller. It is a read-level characterization layer that (a) operates in the LOH/no-phasing regime where the canonical pipeline is blind, (b) preserves molecule-level heterogeneity the pileup destroys, and (c) reframes the result as an existence-spectrum (exists -> locatable -> discriminable) rather than a single region significance call. Its honest negative — methylation is NOT a usable somatic-variant filter — is itself a contribution that the existence-only DMR framing cannot deliver.
pipeline.where_ism_sits: ISM sits ONE LAYER BELOW the DMR call, on the same per-HP haplotagged modBAM that feeds Stage 4/5. After Stage 3 (haplotag -> HP-tagged BAM), the canonical pipeline goes pileup -> bedMethyl -> DSS/modkit-dmr (collapse then 2-group region test). ISM branches at the same HP-tagged BAM but keeps the read x CpG methylation matrix uncollapsed and does read-level distance/clustering (PERMANOVA, ARI, sub-haplotype-matched contrasts). So ISM consumes the identical upstream (Clair3 -> WhatsHap/LongPhase -> haplotag -> Nanopolish/modkit MM-ML calls) but substitutes the terminal 'pileup-collapse + DSS/modkit-dmr region test' with a molecule-resolution analysis, and crucially can also run in the LOH/no-SNV regions where the canonical terminal stages have no input at all.

ism_per_axis.axis: AXIS 1 — Tag/Haplotype-first methylation comparison (phase SNVs -> haplotag reads -> per-HP methylation -> HP1-vs-HP2 aDMR call). The DOMINANT industry approach for ONT allele-specific methylation.
ism_per_axis.ism_position: DOWNSTREAM of this axis's phasing/haplotag backbone, not a replacement for it. ISM consumes HP tags produced by exactly this pipeline (its LOH-constrained longphase-TO/-S variant), so Stages 1-3 (SNV call -> phase -> haplotag) are SHARED. ISM diverges only at Stages 4-5: instead of collapsing each haplotype to a per-CpG mean beta and running a 2-group HP1-vs-HP2 DSS/modkit DMR test, it keeps the full read x CpG matrix and runs a read-distance + PERMANOVA structure engine. ISM does reproduce the canonical site-level statistic (per-CpG Fisher + BH-FDR, Cramer's V + Cochran gate, Delta-beta Wilcoxon + Cohen's d) as a SECONDARY view, but on a different contrast.
ism_per_axis.key_difference: Two structural differences, both verifiable in the C++ (StructureTest.cpp, SignificanceAnalyzer.cpp, RegionProcessor.cpp). (1) UNIT: AXIS 1 tests HP1-mean vs HP2-mean (mean-collapse) and is therefore blind to read-to-read structure / epipolymorphism; ISM's headline is a read-to-read NHD distance matrix -> UPGMA + silhouette -> PERMANOVA pseudo-F (+ dispersion + LabelTest delta=d_between-d_within), which tests whether reads form distinct epigenetic GROUPS. (2) CONTRAST: AXIS 1's HP1-vs-HP2 is intrinsically a GERMLINE allelic axis with somatic specificity handled only by post-hoc imprinting/normal exclusion (O'Neill drops 4.46M raw aDMRs to ~462K). ISM runs a within-engine SOMATIC-CONTROLLED HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis (same parental haplotype, with vs without the somatic event) plus a normal-anchored cis-test (d_cis vs d_drift), so it MEASURES the somatic-vs-germline/copy confound the canonical pipeline can only filter.

ism_per_axis.axis: AXIS 2 — Read-level methylation distance / clustering (read-to-read structure from per-read CpG vectors; FDRP/qFDRP, MeConcord, cvlr, ASMS, modbamtools).
ism_per_axis.ism_position: Squarely ON this axis and arguably its most complete instance for the cancer-somatic case, but NOT alone here. ISM sits in the explicit-distance-matrix sub-family (with FDRP/qFDRP/MeConcord) rather than the model-based-EM sub-family (cvlr/ASMS skip the matrix). Among surveyed tools ISM is the only one combining all four of: explicit read-to-read NHD matrix as primary engine + UPGMA/silhouette group calling + a genuine between-group structure test (PERMANOVA) + a cancer-specific somatic-vs-germline confound control.
ism_per_axis.key_difference: Most peers STOP at a per-CpG/per-bin score (qFDRP, FDRP, MeConcord, Metheor, modbamtools-HDBSCAN) and never test 'is there real read-level structure here?'. ISM adds the PERMANOVA pseudo-F permutation test + dispersion check (so heterogeneity is a tested claim, not a thresholded score). The peers' headline strength — phasing-FREE heterogeneity detection (cvlr/ASMS/modbamtools) — is exactly what makes them unable to separate somatic-cis from germline/imprinting/copy-number; ISM trades that for tag-consuming control (HP1-vs-HP1-1 + normal-anchored cis-test) at the cost of inheriting all upstream LOH-constrained phasing errors. CAVEAT: Metheor is within-read (not read-to-read) so it is mis-grouped if cited as a true peer; ISM's distance engine is O(N^2) like FDRP/UPGMA, so it shares their compute/subsampling-reproducibility weakness.

ism_per_axis.axis: AXIS 3 — Site/region-level DM detection (per-CpG DMP + DMR calling; DSS, methylKit, metilene, dmrseq, DMRcate, comb-p, MOABS, modkit dmr).
ism_per_axis.ism_position: ISM's site-level layer is a METHODOLOGICAL SUBSET of this field and explicitly NOT its primary engine — it is a confirmation/characterization layer. The per-CpG Fisher exact + BH-FDR is essentially methylKit-Fisher; Delta-beta + Cohen's d is an effect-size layer analogous to MOABS CDIF / modkit Cohen's h. ISM adds nothing new to the per-site STATISTIC and is deliberately conservative (Cramer's V is gated to 0 by a Cochran min-expected-count rule, RegionProcessor.cpp ~1592 per memory).
ism_per_axis.key_difference: ISM does NOT compete with this axis on machinery — it is strictly weaker on spatial-correlation handling (no AR(1)/ACF/CBS/kernel smoothing, no principled region-level FDR; dmrseq/comb-p/DMRcate/metilene/DSS all far exceed it) because ISM delegates region structure to its read-distance engine instead of smoothing CpG p-values. Where ISM diverges is the COMPARISON AXIS and POSITION: every AXIS-3 tool runs tumor-group-vs-normal-group and is confounded by ASM/imprinting/mQTL/copy-number/purity (none model CN or purity); ISM runs the haplotype-resolved, somatic-controlled HP1-vs-HP1-1 contrast + normal-anchored cis-test, holding copy-number/ploidy/alignment constant by design. Honest framing: this is a confound-control + positioning difference, not a new per-site test.

ism_per_axis.axis: AXIS 4 — Methylation-based discrimination / classification (what the signal discriminates: allele vs tissue-of-origin vs tumor-fraction vs expression-driver vs true/false variant).
ism_per_axis.ism_position: ISM asked a target NOBODY else in the survey directly tests — can ASM signal discriminate TRUE vs FALSE somatic VARIANT calls (a variant-QC filter)? — and answered a definitive NEGATIVE four independent ways. ISM is therefore on AXIS 4 only as a deliberate falsification: it reframes from filter to CHARACTERIZATION. The surveyed tools each target a DIFFERENT discrimination question (allele: DAMEfinder/CGmapTools/amrfinder; tissue: MHB/MHL/CancerLocator; fraction: CancerLocator; driver: MethylMix/ELMER).
ism_per_axis.key_difference: The contribution here is an HONEST NEGATIVE, not a solved gap: ASM is real but anti-discriminative — strong-ASM is ~5x ENRICHED in FP (OR=0.194, p=1.8e-28, per evidence ledger / memory), and methylation tested as a TP/FP filter failed 4 ways (LR sample-level circularity, low ~4% sensitivity, COLO829 TP approx FP, cis HP_Residual FP highest). Genuine methodological differences vs the field: (1) SNP-anchored peers compare REF-vs-ALT (germline/imprinting-confounded ALLELE axis; ISM's own ALLELE-axis test gave TP 11.1% < het-null 15.2%); ISM uniquely builds the somatic-controlled HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis. (2) ISM adds the normal-anchored cis-test that operationalizes the 'heterogeneity vs real ASM' problem DAMEfinder names as unsolved. (3) ISM's primary discriminator is a multivariate read-cluster PERMANOVA, which no surveyed tool has (closest analogues — amrfinder's 2-component LRT, DAMEfinder's CpG-pair tuple — are far simpler).

axis_oneliners: AXIS 1 — Tag/haplotype-first: phase germline het SNVs -> haplotag reads -> collapse to per-haplotype mean methylation -> call HP1-vs-HP2 aDMRs; the dominant ONT allele-specific-methylation pipeline (NanoMethPhase/modkit/DSS/POG), and the backbone ISM sits downstream of.

AXIS 2 — Read-level distance/clustering: build a read x CpG matrix and compare reads to each other (explicit NHD distance + clustering, or model-based EM mixtures) to detect epiallele/subclonal structure; ISM's home axis and arguably its most complete cancer-somatic instance.

AXIS 3 — Site/region-level DM detection: per-CpG count-model test (beta-binomial/Fisher) + multiple-testing + spatial aggregation -> ranked DMRs; a mature toolkit (DSS/dmrseq/DMRcate/...) that ISM mirrors only as a conservative secondary site layer.

AXIS 4 — Discrimination/classification: use methylation to discriminate a chosen target (allele / tissue-of-origin / tumor-fraction / expression-driver); ISM uniquely asked the variant-QC target (true-vs-false somatic call) and got a definitive NEGATIVE, reframing to characterization.
common_difficulties: PHASING DEPENDENCE + LOH erases het anchors (cancer-specific, severe): every haplotype-resolved method (AXIS 1 fully, AXIS 3 somatic-framing, ISM, ASMS) is downstream of correctly phased het SNVs. SNP deserts -> reads untagged; switch-errors silently swap HP1/HP2 and fake or destroy aDMRs; block N50 caps co-attribution distance. LOH/cnLOH DELETE one allele's het SNVs, so the most cancer-relevant regions (deleted tumor suppressors: CDKN2A, BRCA1, NF1, RB1 — O'Neill could fully phase these in only ~half of tumors) lose anchors precisely where ASM matters. ISM inherits all of this from its LOH-constrained phasing.

GERMLINE-vs-SOMATIC confound (imprinting + cis-haplotype ASM masquerade as cancer ASM): HP1-vs-HP2 and REF-vs-ALT are intrinsically GERMLINE axes mixing ~150 imprinted domains, random monoallelic methylation, and germline mQTL. A significant allelic difference is NOT automatically tumor-acquired. The field handles it only by post-hoc exclusion against a matched normal (discards signal, can't catch somatic events landing on imprinted loci). This is the central trap and ISM's main raison d'etre (HP1-vs-HP1-1 + normal-anchored cis-test), but ISM does not eliminate it — it depends on the LOH-constrained tags being right.

COPY-NUMBER / LOH drives APPARENT allelic methylation arithmetically (CNA confound): a CN change shifts the methylated/unmethylated allele RATIO with ZERO epigenetic change (4:1 amplification -> 75:25 'methylation'); Martin-Trujillo 2017 showed CNAs explain MOST apparent imprinting aberration (only 8-17.6% of imprinted regions show CN-independent change). cnLOH makes both 'haplotypes' derive from one parental allele. No standard AXIS-1/3/4 tool models CN; CAMDAC formalizes the deconvolution. ISM's defense is held-constant CN/ploidy on the HP1-vs-HP1-1 axis + cis-test, but absolute effect sizes can still be CN-flavored.

TUMOR PURITY / normal-cell admixture: observed beta = p*tumor + (1-p)*normal, so low purity drags somatic hyper/hypo-methylation toward 50/50, shrinking Delta-beta below the |0.1| call gate (a real ASM in a 30%-pure sample can be invisible) AND inflates read-level heterogeneity scores (admixture LOOKS heterogeneous; qFDRP predicts purity at r=0.966). A hard floor on every axis including ISM's PERMANOVA structure call.

COVERAGE / POWER, worse per-haplotype: read-level + ASM metrics have hard floors (FDRP/qFDRP need ~10x/CpG and >=4 co-covered CpGs; PDR needs >=4 CpGs/read; EM mixtures need enough reads/cluster). Haplotagging HALVES depth per pile, so reliable ASM needs ~2x bulk coverage (NANOME: >=15x/HP ~= >=30x total). Per-CpG binomial noise scales 1/sqrt(n). Hits ISM's distance/cluster estimates and its site-level Cochran gate equally.

SINGLE-SAMPLE statistical power / pseudo-replication: cancer ONT studies typically have ONE tumor (+/- one normal), no biological replicates, so you cannot separate biological from sampling variance; per-CpG tests treating read counts as replicates are pseudo-replication at the patient level (DSS-single borrows spatial neighbors as pseudo-reps to partly fix it). Single-sample positives can't be distinguished from sample-specific idiosyncrasy/circularity — exactly why ISM's single-sample HCC1395 results are tier-capped (single-pipeline -> ceiling ~star-3) and need cross-sample/held-out replication.

HETEROGENEITY / EPIPOLYMORPHISM collapses under mean-based methods: a tumor is a subclone mixture, so 50% methylation can mean half the cells fully methylated, not a hemi-methylated allele. PDR/epipolymorphism/FDRP quantify this, but any per-haplotype or per-group MEAN beta (all of AXIS 1, all of AXIS 3) sees a beta not a distribution and is structurally blind to it. This is the blind spot ISM's read-distance engine exists to fill — but heterogeneity also CONFOUNDS ISM (admixture/coverage inflate apparent structure), so a positive PERMANOVA is not automatically somatic-subclonal.

5mC vs 5hmC conflation: bisulfite cannot separate them (all surveyed bisulfite-era tools lump 5mC+5hmC); 5hmC is globally depleted in many tumors with often-opposite regulatory meaning, so a 'methylation difference' can be a 5mC<->5hmC swap. ONT MM/ML carries both but per-read 5mC-vs-5hmC separation is the hardest call, and naive max-collapse over the two channels can halve/distort the per-position fraction (this exact artifact bit ISM once: a buggy MSA Level-1 double-column halved BRCA2 Delta-beta to -0.054 vs the correct -0.122).

REGION-DEFINITION / METRIC arbitrariness: DMR boundaries depend on smoothing bandwidth / HMM segmentation / |Delta-beta|>=0.1 + min-CpG heuristics (AXIS 3), and read-distance results depend on the distance metric (NHD over co-covered CpGs is biased by missing data, overlap length, CpG density, read length — qFDRP/LPMD were invented to fix FDRP's read-length bias). Same data -> different aDMR/cluster counts under different settings.

BISULFITE-ERA / SHORT-READ TOOL-CONTEXT MISMATCH: FDRP/qFDRP, MeConcord, Metheor, DAMEfinder, CGmapTools, amrfinder, MHB/MHL were built/benchmarked on short bisulfite reads (35-150bp, CpG-only, no 5hmC, few co-CpG/read). ONT long reads (5mC+5hmC, multi-kb spans, many het SNPs + CpGs on one molecule) are OUTSIDE their design envelope; re-implementing tuple/MHL/read-pair logic on long reads is non-trivial and is where ISM operates natively.
what_ism_uniquely_adds: A SOMATIC-CONTROLLED haplotype contrast (HP1 germline vs HP1-1 somatic-on-same-haplotype) rather than the field-standard germline HP1-vs-HP2 or REF-vs-ALT. This is the one genuinely structural novelty: every surveyed tool's allelic axis is germline and handles somatic specificity only by post-hoc normal/imprinting exclusion; ISM builds the within-engine somatic-vs-its-germline-counterpart axis directly (verified in the LOH-constrained tag scheme HP1/HP1-1/HP2/HP2-1).

A NORMAL-ANCHORED cis-test (normal-HP1 baseline; d_cis vs d_drift) that MEASURES — rather than merely filters — the somatic-cis vs germline-drift/copy confound, operationalizing the 'heterogeneity vs real ASM' problem DAMEfinder explicitly calls unsolved. Narrow caveat: it is single-sample and tag-dependent, so it constrains rather than fully resolves the confound.

A read-level multivariate STRUCTURE TEST as the headline output (read x CpG NHD distance -> UPGMA + silhouette -> PERMANOVA pseudo-F with permutation + dispersion + LabelTest delta=d_between-d_within), confirmed in src/core/StructureTest.cpp + HierarchicalClustering.cpp + SignificanceAnalyzer.cpp. Among surveyed tools, only ISM pairs an explicit distance matrix with a genuine between-group permutation test (peers either stop at a per-CpG score or use model-based EM with a fixed/unselected K and no structure test).

An HONEST, hard NEGATIVE that is itself the contribution: methylation/ASM is real but NOT a usable TP/FP somatic-variant filter — failed 4 independent ways, and strong-ASM is ANTI-discriminative (~5x enriched in FP, OR=0.194, p=1.8e-28; corroborated in the evidence ledger and memory). No surveyed tool asks the variant-QC question, so this is a gap-closing falsification, not a gap others already solved.

A conservative, gated site layer wired to the same data: per-CpG Fisher + BH-FDR with Cramer's V zeroed by a Cochran minimum-expected-count gate (RegionProcessor.cpp), which deliberately suppresses spurious significance from sparse 2x2 tables — a discipline most fast DMR callers skip. Honest scope: this is a guardrail, not a new statistic.
what_ism_lacks_vs_others: NO principled spatial region aggregation / region-level FDR. The entire AXIS-3 field far exceeds ISM here: dmrseq AR(1), comb-p ACF-weighted Stouffer-Liptak + Sidak, DMRcate Gaussian kernel, metilene CBS segmentation, BSmooth/DSS local smoothing. ISM does per-CpG BH-FDR but delegates region structure to its read-distance engine, so it cannot produce calibrated DMR boundaries or genome-wide region FDR the way standard callers do.

NO new or stronger per-site STATISTIC. ISM's Fisher + Delta-beta + Cohen's d is a strict subset of (and weaker than) DSS/MOABS/methylKit/modkit: no beta-binomial over-dispersion model, no empirical-Bayes dispersion shrinkage, no biological-variance handling — the things that make single-sample DM honest. ISM's site layer is intentionally conservative, but that means it is statistically less powerful, not more.

NO phasing-FREE mode. cvlr, ASMS, modbamtools, FDRP/qFDRP, MeConcord all detect read-level structure WITHOUT needing HP tags. ISM's somatic-controlled axis is entirely contingent on upstream LOH-constrained phasing/haplotagging, so in SNP-deserts / LOH / low-het regions it simply has no signal where phasing-free peers can still cluster reads.

NO copy-number / purity DECONVOLUTION. CAMDAC explicitly infers purity + allele-specific CN and inverts the mixture model to recover pure-tumor allele-specific methylation; CancerLocator jointly MLEs tumor fraction. ISM holds CN constant by DESIGN (HP1-vs-HP1-1) but does not estimate or correct purity/CN, so its absolute effect sizes can still be CN/purity-flavored and it cannot report a deconvolved pure-tumor rate.

NO cohort / cross-sample inference engine, and NO tissue-of-origin / deconvolution / expression-driver capability. MethylMix (Beta-mixture states, ~>=100 samples), ELMER (enhancer-gene + TF-motif), MHB/MHL + CancerLocator (reference-panel deconvolution) all do things ISM does not attempt. ISM is single-tumor and tier-capped at ~star-3 for single-pipeline single-sample work, and recurrence/cohort confidence (e.g. POG's 189-sample aDMR recurrence) is exactly what it lacks.

NO scale advantage and a known O(N^2) cost / reproducibility weakness. The explicit read-to-read distance matrix + UPGMA is O(N^2)-O(N^3) and shares the read-pair WSH subsampling problem (subsampling makes results non-reproducible across runs). Model-based peers (cvlr/ASMS) sidestep the matrix entirely. ISM also remains validated mostly on single samples (HCC1395) with limited cross-platform breadth (COLO829/DORADO/H2009 partly pending).
